senses.title: A chain folded into a working shape
senses.titleCN: 蛋白质：折叠成形的氨基酸链
senses.definition: a macromolecule made of one or more chains of amino acids folded into a defined three-dimensional shape
senses.definitionCN: 由一条或多条氨基酸链折叠成确定三维形状的生物大分子
senses.example: Haemoglobin is a protein built from four folded chains.
senses.exampleCN: 血红蛋白是由四条折叠链构成的蛋白质。
senses.why: Greek prōteios meant 'primary', and the name was given because such substances were thought to be the primary stuff of nutrition; the modern molecule sense grew from that label.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 prōteios 意为「首要的」，命名时认为这类物质是营养的首要成分；现代「分子」义正是在这个标签上发展出来的。

senses.title: Sequence and fold
senses.definition: the internal plan of a protein: the order of amino acids and the way that order folds
senses.definitionCN: 蛋白质的内部方案：氨基酸的排列顺序，以及这一顺序折叠的方式
senses.example: A single wrong amino acid can spoil the fold of the whole protein.
senses.exampleCN: 一个氨基酸出错就可能毁掉整个蛋白质的折叠。
senses.why: once the chain was sequenced, the word covered not only the substance but the architecture that makes it work.
senses.whyCN: 当链被测序后，这个词不仅指物质，也指让它工作的构造。

senses.title: The nutrient on a plate
senses.titleCN: 营养义：膳食中的蛋白质
senses.definition: the component of food that supplies amino acids, spoken of in amounts and quality
senses.definitionCN: 食物中提供氨基酸的成分，常按数量与质量来谈
senses.example: Beans and rice together supply a complete set of protein.
senses.exampleCN: 豆类与米饭搭配可提供完整的蛋白质。
senses.why: because the molecule is what the body rebuilds from food, the same word names the nutrient class on the plate.
senses.whyCN: 因为身体正是用食物重建这种分子，同一个词也指盘中的那类营养素。

senses.title: A job description, not a shape
senses.titleCN: 功能类别：按工作分工的蛋白质
senses.definition: a class of molecules grouped by what they do, such as enzymes, structural proteins, transporters and signals
senses.definitionCN: 按功能归类的分子，如酶、结构蛋白、运输蛋白与信号蛋白
senses.example: Collagen is a structural protein; insulin is a signal protein.
senses.exampleCN: 胶原蛋白是结构蛋白；胰岛素是信号蛋白。
senses.why: since shape serves a task, the word is also used to sort proteins by the task rather than by the fold.
senses.whyCN: 由于形状服务于任务，这个词也被用来按任务而非按折叠方式给蛋白质分类。

senses.title: Measured in a lab
senses.titleCN: 表达与水平：实验中的蛋白量
senses.definition: the amount of a particular protein made by a cell or sample, as measured in experiments
senses.definitionCN: 细胞或样本中某种特定蛋白质的生成量，以实验方式测定
senses.example: The tumour showed high protein expression of the receptor.
senses.exampleCN: 该肿瘤中受体的蛋白表达量很高。
senses.why: laboratory practice turns the substance into a quantity, so 'protein' can mean a measured level rather than a molecule.
senses.whyCN: 实验室实践把这种物质变成一种量，因此 protein 可以指被测定的水平，而非分子本身。

senses.title: Separated and detected
senses.titleCN: 纯化与检测：实验台上的蛋白操作
senses.definition: the substance as an object of purification, blotting and detection
senses.definitionCN: 作为纯化、印迹与检测对象的该物质
senses.example: The protein was purified from bacterial cultures and run on a gel.
senses.exampleCN: 该蛋白从细菌培养物中纯化，并在凝胶上电泳。
senses.why: methods name their object by the material, so a gel band or a blot is simply called protein.
senses.whyCN: 方法学以其材料来命名对象，因此凝胶条带或印迹就被直接称为 protein。

senses.title: The whole set at once
senses.definition: the entire complement of proteins in a cell or tissue, studied as a set
senses.definitionCN: 细胞或组织中全部蛋白质的总体，作为一个集合来研究
senses.example: Proteomic analysis compares thousands of proteins between healthy and sick tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 蛋白质组分析比较健康与患病组织间数千种蛋白质。
senses.why: high-throughput methods made the collective countable, so the singular word can also stand for the whole set.
senses.whyCN: 高通量方法使这个集合变得可计数，因此单数形式也可指整个集合。

senses.title: Designed and rebuilt
senses.titleCN: 蛋白质工程：改造与设计
senses.definition: a molecule treated as something that can be redesigned, fused or synthesized
senses.definitionCN: 被当作可以重新设计、融合或合成的分子的蛋白质
senses.example: Engineers added a tag to the protein so it could be captured.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师给该蛋白加了一个标签，以便把它捕获。
senses.why: when folding is understood as a code, the substance becomes a design space, and the word follows it there.
senses.whyCN: 当折叠被理解为一种编码，这种物质就成了设计空间，这个词也随之进入该用法。

intro.en: Protein was coined in 1838 from Greek prōteios 'primary', a word built on prōtos 'first'. It reached English through French protéine.
intro.cn: protein 于 1838 年由希腊 prōteios「首要的」造出，该词基于 prōtos「第一」。它经法语 protéine 进入英语。

items.en: prōtos meant 'first, foremost', and prōteios 'primary, of the first rank'. The compound behind them is a Greek formation, not a Latin one.
items.cn: prōtos 意为「第一、最前」，prōteios 意为「首要的、第一等的」。其背后的构词属希腊语，不是拉丁语。

items.en: Jöns Jacob Berzelius proposed the name protéine for the substance Mulder described as a primary constituent of living matter. The date is well recorded; the exact wording of the proposal is not.
items.cn: Jöns Jacob Berzelius 为 Mulder 所述「生命物质的首要成分」提议了 protéine 这一名称。年份有明确记录，提议的原话则无存。

items.en: Generally thought: the name reflects the belief that this substance was the primary material of nutrition and of the body; the reasoning is reported second-hand and not fully documented.
items.cn: 一般认为，这个名字反映了当时认为该物质是营养与身体的首要材料；其推理为二手记载，并未完整留存。

items.en: English protein appears in the nineteenth century through French; the earliest citation is approximate.
items.cn: 英语 protein 于 19 世纪经法语传入；最早书证年代为约数。

items.en: Twentieth-century chemistry established the amino acid chain and the folded structure, widening the word from a substance to an architecture.
items.cn: 20 世纪的化学确立了氨基酸链与折叠结构，把该词从一种物质扩展到一种构造。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the origin of prōtos before Greek is unsettled, and any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction; the earliest English date for protein is also approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：prōtos 在希腊语之前的来源并无定论，凡给出的印欧形式均属重构；protein 的最早英语书证亦为约数。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes that are often mistaken for relatives; group two holds words that name related molecules or roles.
note.cn: 第一组是常被误认为同族的形近词；第二组是命名相关分子或角色的词。

entries.definition: Means 'ever-changing, versatile', from Proteus, the shape-shifting sea god. It shares letters with protein but comes from a different Greek name.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「多变、多才多艺」，来自会变形的海神 Proteus；与 protein 只是拼写相近，来源是另一个希腊专名。

entries.definition: A protein-digesting enzyme. It is named with -ase 'enzyme', so it is a tool that acts on proteins.
entries.definitionCN: 指分解蛋白质的酶；由 -ase「酶」构成，是作用于蛋白质的工具。

entries.definition: All the proteins of a cell or tissue, named with -ome 'complete set'. It is a collection, not one molecule.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个细胞或组织的全部蛋白质，由 -ome「全集」构成；是集合，不是单个分子。

entries.definition: A short amino acid chain, from Greek peptos 'digested', not from prōtos. Peptides are shorter than proteins.
entries.definitionCN: 指短氨基酸链，来自希腊 peptos「被消化的」，并非 prōtos；肽比蛋白质短。

entries.definition: A long chain of amino acids before folding is considered; a protein is the folded, working object.
entries.definitionCN: 指尚未考虑折叠的长氨基酸链；protein 指折叠后能工作的对象。

entries.definition: A catalyst made of protein or RNA. Many enzymes are proteins, but not all proteins are enzymes.
entries.definitionCN: 由蛋白质或 RNA 构成的催化剂；许多酶是蛋白质，但并非所有蛋白质都是酶。

entries.definition: The single building block; a protein is a chain of them.
entries.definitionCN: 单个构建单元；蛋白质是由它们连成的链。

entries.definition: Any substance that nourishes. Protein is one nutrient among several, alongside fat and carbohydrate.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何提供营养的物质；蛋白质是与脂肪、碳水化合物并列的一种营养素。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: prōteios 'primary': the substance once thought to be the first stuff of the body.
normal.cn: prōteios「首要的」：这曾被当作身体的第一种材料。

normal.en: The family runs protein, proteome, proteomics, proteinase, proteolysis.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 protein、proteome、proteomics、proteinase、proteolysis。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: protein structure, protein folding, protein expression, protein purification.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：蛋白质结构、折叠、表达、纯化。

normal.en: A protein is a chain that folds; a peptide is a short chain; an enzyme is one kind of protein.
normal.cn: 蛋白质是折叠的链；肽是短链；酶是蛋白质的一种。

normal.en: Structure decides function: the fold makes the pocket, and the pocket decides the partner.
normal.cn: 结构决定功能：折叠造出凹槽，凹槽决定结合对象。

abstract.en: Picture a necklace of coloured beads crushed into a ball with dents and ridges.
abstract.cn: 想象一条彩色珠链被揉成一团，表面有凹坑与凸棱。

abstract.en: Picture a key that is also made of beads, so its shape can be rewritten bead by bead.
abstract.cn: 想象一把也由珠子构成的钥匙，其形状可以逐颗改写。

abstract.en: Picture a kitchen where the same ingredient is used as fuel, as brick and as signal.
abstract.cn: 想象一间厨房，同一种材料既当燃料，又当砖块，还当信号。

examples.en: Heating denatures the protein, so the egg white turns solid.
examples.cn: 加热使蛋白质变性，因此蛋白凝固。

examples.en: Athletes often eat more protein than they strictly need.
examples.cn: 运动员常摄入超过实际所需的蛋白质。

examples.en: The protein was tagged with a fluorescent label for imaging.
examples.cn: 该蛋白被加上荧光标签以便成像。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑（pro）上去的（tein）一团」——氨基酸连成链再揉成一团，构成身体的首要材料 → 蛋白质

root: 希腊 prōtos「第一」→ prōteios「首要的」→ 法语 protéine（1838，Berzelius 提议）→ 英语 protein。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a chain folds into a shape, and that shape is then read as an architecture, a nutrient, a job class, a measured level, a laboratory object, a whole set, and finally a design space.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：一条链折叠成一个形状，而这个形状依次被读成构造、营养素、岗位类别、测定值、实验对象、全集，最后是设计空间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bead chain crumpled into a lump whose dents fit one partner.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条珠链被揉成团块，其凹处只与一个对象相合。

branches.en: THE MOLECULE: the folded chain is the basic referent of the word.
branches.cn: 分子本身：折叠的链是该词的基本所指。

branches.en: ARCHITECTURE: sequence plus fold, the plan behind the shape.
branches.cn: 构造：序列加折叠，即形状背后的方案。

branches.en: NUTRIENT: the same substance read as food on a plate.
branches.cn: 营养素：同一种物质被读成盘中的食物。

branches.en: JOB CLASS: proteins sorted by task rather than by fold.
branches.cn: 岗位类别：按任务而非按折叠方式分类的蛋白质。

branches.en: QUANTITY AND DESIGN: measured levels, bench objects, whole sets, and molecules rewritten by engineers.
branches.cn: 数量与设计：测定水平、实验台对象、全集，以及被工程师改写的分子。

intro.en: Protein is a Greek-derived noun carrying a Greek suffix -eios; English adds the usual Latin-based endings for its family.
intro.cn: protein 是带希腊后缀 -eios 的希腊派生名词；英语为其词族加上通常的拉丁式词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no classical Latin source. New Latin proteinum is a Latinized spelling, while -ase, -ome and proteo- are modern scientific combining forms.
latinIntro.cn: 没有古典拉丁来源。新拉丁语 proteinum 是拉丁化拼写，而 -ase、-ome 与 proteo- 是现代科学组合形式。

items.meaning: the primary substance of nutrition; a folded amino acid chain
items.meaningCN: 营养的首要物质；折叠的氨基酸链
items.example: The protein binds calcium at its centre.
Membrane proteins transport ions across the bilayer.
items.exampleCN: 膜蛋白把离子运过脂双层。

items.meaningCN: 由蛋白质构成的；蛋白状的
items.example: A proteinaceous coat surrounds the spore.
items.exampleCN: 一层蛋白性质的外壳包裹着孢子。

items.example: A serine proteinase digests the collagen.
items.exampleCN: 一种丝氨酸蛋白酶消化胶原。
蛋白质水解会释放出活性激素。

items.meaning: all proteins of a cell or tissue
items.meaningCN: 细胞或组织的全部蛋白质
items.exampleCN: 蛋白质组会随压力改变。

items.meaningCN: 大规模研究蛋白质的学科
items.exampleCN: 蛋白质组学需要灵敏的质谱仪。

items.example: Only proteogenic amino acids enter the chain.
items.exampleCN: 只有生蛋白氨基酸能进入链中。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 蛋白质（拉丁化科学名称）

definition_zh: 抗议；抗议活动；反对；申辩；坚称
definition_en: a public statement or action showing strong disagreement, the act of objecting in public, or a firm declaration that something is true
core_image: 一群人举着写满字的纸牌站在门前，谁都不肯散去
scene: 新规定贴出来的第二天清晨，居民们举着纸牌站到办公楼前，没有人愿意走开。Hundreds of residents gathered outside the office to protest against the new rule.
sceneCN: 这里表示「抗议、反对」（第 2 个义项：公开表达强烈反对）；句意为数百名居民聚在办公楼外，抗议这条新规定。

pos.zh: 抗议；抗议活动；异议
抗议；反对；申辩；坚称

derivatives.zh: 由 protest 加表示施动者的 -er 构成，义为「抗议者」
由拉丁词干 protestat- 加 -ion 构成，义为「声明；抗议」，语气正式
由 protesting 加 -ly 构成，义为「带着抗议地；不服地」

senses.title: A public expression of strong disagreement
senses.definition: a statement, gathering or march by which people show in public that they refuse to accept a decision or a situation
senses.definitionCN: 人们用声明、集会或游行的方式，公开表示不接受某项决定或某种状况
senses.example: The sit-in was a quiet protest against the closure of the library.
senses.exampleCN: 那次静坐是对关闭图书馆的一场无声抗议。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to declare something publicly and call others to witness it; when the declaration is a refusal, the noun becomes the event in the street.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为公开声明并请人作证；当声明的内容是「不接受」时，名词就成了街头上的那场活动。

senses.title: To state in public that one objects
senses.definition: to say openly, often together with others, that something is wrong and ought to be changed
senses.definitionCN: 公开说出自己认为某事不对、应当改变，常与众人一起
senses.example: Villagers protested against the plan to dam the river.
senses.exampleCN: 村民抗议在河上筑坝的计划。
senses.why: The same public declaration is now seen as an action rather than an event, so the verb keeps the crowd and the refusal but adds the doing.
senses.whyCN: 同一场公开声明被看成动作而不是事件，于是动词保留了人群与拒绝，只是多了一层「正在做」。

senses.title: To insist firmly that something is true
senses.definition: to say firmly that something is the case, especially when denying a charge or correcting what others believe
senses.definitionCN: 坚定地说某事就是这样，尤用于否认指控或纠正别人的看法
senses.example: He protested that he had never signed the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他坚称自己从未签过那份文件。
senses.why: Before it meant to object, the Latin verb simply meant to bear witness; that older layer survives whenever a person protests innocence rather than protesting a policy.
senses.whyCN: 在表示「反对」之前，这个拉丁动词只表示「作证」；一个人申辩自己无罪而不是抗议某项政策时，留下的正是那更早的一层。

intro.en: Protest goes back to a Latin verb for bearing witness in public; English first used it for a solemn declaration and only later for a refusal.
intro.cn: protest 可追到拉丁语中「公开作证」的动词；英语最初用它指郑重的声明，后来才用来指拒绝接受。

items.en: Testis meant a witness, the person who can stand up and say what happened.
items.cn: testis 意为证人，即那个能站出来说出发生了什么的人。

items.en: Testari meant to bear witness or to call someone as a witness, and it grew out of testis.
items.cn: testari 意为作证或请人作证，由 testis 派生而来。

items.en: With pro-, the witnessing moved into the open, so protestari meant to declare something publicly and solemnly.
items.cn: 加上 pro-，作证被推到公开场合，于是 protestari 意为公开而郑重地声明。

items.en: Old French borrowed the word as protest, a solemn declaration, and passed it into English around the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语借入后写作 protest，意为郑重声明，约在十四世纪传入英语。

items.en: English kept the old sense of declaring, then added the modern one of objecting in public, and finally the quieter sense of insisting that one is right.
items.cn: 英语保留了「声明」的旧义，又添上「公开反对」的新义，最后还有「坚称自己没错」这层更安静的意思。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin witness and the declaration built on it; the second group gathers words for objecting and for stating a grievance.
note.cn: 第一组共用拉丁语的「证人」及由此构成的「声明」；第二组收表示反对与诉说不满的词。

entries.definition: A formal declaration, especially one that objects to something.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的声明，尤指表示反对的声明。

entries.definition: To give evidence as a witness, from the same Latin word for witness.
entries.definitionCN: 作为证人提供证词，出自同一个表示「证人」的拉丁词。

entries.definition: A formal statement given by a witness in court.
entries.definitionCN: 证人在法庭上作出的正式陈述。

entries.definition: To keep someone safe; the prefix pro- is shared, but the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 保护某人；只是拼写相近，词源不同，两者只共用前缀 pro-。

entries.definition: To say that you disagree with something.
entries.definitionCN: 表示不同意某事。

entries.definition: To gather in public in order to show opposition or support.
entries.definitionCN: 公开聚集以表示反对或支持。

entries.definition: A statement that something is wrong, often made to an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 指出某事有问题的说法，常向当局提出。

entries.definition: A loud public expression of anger or disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 公众大声表达的愤怒或不满。

normalIntro.en: Every sense keeps the Latin witness: someone stands up in the open and says what he or she will not accept or will not admit.
normalIntro.cn: 每个义项都留着那个拉丁语的「证人」：有人站到明处，说出自己不接受或不承认的事。

normal.en: Pro- means forth and testis means witness, so protest is to bring a witness's statement out into public.
normal.cn: pro- 意为向前、公开，testis 意为证人，所以 protest 就是把证人的话拿到公开场合说出来。

normal.en: Testify, testimony and protest all keep that witness, which is why a courtroom and a street march can share one root.
normal.cn: testify、testimony 与 protest 都保留着这个「证人」，所以法庭与街头游行能共用一个词根。

normal.en: The noun names the event and the verb names the doing, yet both need other people to hear the refusal.
normal.cn: 名词指那场活动，动词指正在做的动作，但两者都需要别人听见这份拒绝。

normal.en: Protesting that you are innocent keeps the oldest sense, because there the word is still a declaration rather than a complaint.
normal.cn: 申辩自己无罪保留的是最古老的那层意思，因为那里它仍是声明，而不是抱怨。

normal.en: The stress moves with the part of speech in British English, and that shift alone tells a listener whether the word is the event or the act.
normal.cn: 英式英语里重音随词性移动，单是这一变化就能让听者知道这个词指事件还是动作。

abstract.en: A protest asks to be heard before it asks to be obeyed, which is why it lives in the open air.
abstract.cn: 抗议先求被听见，才求被采纳，所以它总发生在露天的场所。

abstract.en: The same word covers refusal and declaration because both are a person standing up and saying what is true for them.
abstract.cn: 同一个词兼指拒绝与声明，因为两者都是同一个人站出来，说出对他而言为真的事。

abstract.en: When a protest is ignored it tends to grow louder, while a declaration that is believed goes quiet, and one word holds both ends.
abstract.cn: 抗议被忽视时往往更响，声明被相信时反而安静，同一个词却装着这两端。

examples.en: Thousands joined the protest outside the town hall.
examples.cn: 数千人参加了市政厅外的抗议。

examples.en: They protested against the rise in bus fares.
examples.cn: 他们抗议公交车票价上涨。

examples.en: She protested that she had never met him.
examples.cn: 她坚称自己从未见过他。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若泰斯特」——声音先「普」地一下炸开，再「泰斯特」地念出不满；记住 protest 是抗议、反对。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前、公开）+ testis（证人）→ testari（作证）→ protestari（公开声明、郑重宣称）→ 古法语 protest，约十四世纪进入英语。最早指「郑重声明」，后来才指「公开反对」。注意 protest 与 protect 只共用前缀 pro-：protect 的词根是 tegere（覆盖），protest 的词根是 testis（证人）。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a public declaration; the senses divide into the event of objecting, the act of objecting, and the older sense of insisting on the truth.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「公开声明」；义项由此分出作为事件的抗议、作为动作的反对，以及更古老的「坚称事实」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd holding signs in front of a door, saying aloud what they will not accept.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群人举着纸牌站在门前，把不肯接受的事大声说出来。

branches.en: a row of signs lifted above a crowd
branches.cn: 人群上方举起的一排纸牌

branches.en: a chant rising outside a closed office
branches.cn: 紧闭的办公楼外响起整齐的喊声

branches.en: a man repeating that he never signed
branches.cn: 一个人反复说自己从未签过字

branches.en: one refusal spoken and acted at the same time
branches.cn: 同一份拒绝既被说出又被行动

branches.en: a word that objects and a word that swears
branches.cn: 一个既在反对又在申明的词

intro.en: A Latin noun for witness, a prefix that brings the statement into public, and the English endings that make the doer and the formal noun hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示「证人」的拉丁名词、把声明带到公开场合的前缀，以及造出「人」与正式名词的英语词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Testis, testari and protestari are the reliable Latin cognates; the same witness root also appears in testimony and testify.
latinIntro.cn: testis、testari 与 protestari 是可靠的同源词；同一个「证人」词根也出现在 testimony 与 testify 里。

definition_zh: 协议；礼仪；规程；实验方案；计算机协议
definition_en: the first sheet of a document, and by extension the formal rules — diplomatic, scientific, medical, or digital — that govern how people and machines deal with one another
core_image: 一卷羊皮纸的开头贴着一张写满条目的小纸片，规定这份文件如何被读、被签、被遵守
scene: 一位年轻外交官在签到台前被告知要按顺序签名。Protocol requires diplomats to sign in the order of rank.
sceneCN: 这里 protocol 是「礼仪、礼节」（第 2 个义项：外交或仪式中公认的正式行为与位次规则）；句意：按礼节来，按顺序签字，绝不要抢在大使之前发言。画面里有长桌、座椅次序和一份摊开的文件；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 协议；议定书；礼仪；规程；实验方案；（计算机）协议

derivatives.zh: 礼仪的；协议的（较少用）
礼宾官；协议起草者（罕用）
使规程化；将……纳入协议（技术用语）
已记入议定书的（英式拼写）
记录议定书；按规程处理

senses.title: The treaty on paper: a formal agreement
senses.titleCN: 协议、议定书：写在纸上的正式约定
senses.definition: a formal agreement or treaty, especially one between states or organizations
senses.definitionCN: 正式的协议或条约，尤指国家或组织之间的
senses.example: The two governments signed a protocol on border patrols.
senses.exampleCN: 两国政府签署了一份关于边境巡逻的议定书。
senses.why: From the 1540s sense 'draft of a document, original of any writing', a protocol became the official record of a transaction. When that record is signed by friendly powers, the sheet of paper is the agreement itself.
senses.whyCN: 从 16 世纪 40 年代“文件草稿、任何文书的原件”这一义项起，protocol 成为交易的官方记录。当这份记录由友好国家签署，那张纸本身就是协议。

senses.title: The order of the room: diplomatic etiquette
senses.titleCN: 礼仪、礼节：房间里谁先谁后
senses.definition: the accepted rules of formal behavior and precedence in diplomacy or ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 外交或仪式中公认的正式行为与位次规则
senses.example: The young attaché was criticized for breaking protocol.
senses.exampleCN: 那位年轻随员因违反礼节而受到批评。
senses.why: French extended the word to 'formula of diplomatic etiquette', attested in English by 1896. The first sheet of a treaty recorded the order of ceremony, so the sheet became the order itself.
senses.whyCN: 法语把这个词扩展为“外交礼仪的程式”，1896 年在英语中出现。条约的首张贴纸记录仪式次序，于是那张纸就变成了次序本身。

senses.title: The prescribed steps: an operating procedure
senses.titleCN: 规程：一步一步照做的那套规矩
senses.definition: an official procedure or set of rules for carrying out a task
senses.definitionCN: 执行某项任务的官方程序或规则
senses.example: Staff must follow the safety protocol when handling chemicals.
senses.exampleCN: 员工处理化学品时必须遵守安全规程。
senses.why: Once protocol means the official record of how something is done, it easily means the prescribed way to do it. The written order of a ceremony becomes the written order of any operation.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 protocol 指“某事如何进行的官方记录”，它就很容易指“规定的进行方式”。仪式的书面次序，变成了任何操作的书面次序。

senses.title: The plan of the experiment
senses.titleCN: 实验方案：写在前面的研究步骤
senses.definition: a detailed written plan for a scientific experiment or clinical trial
senses.definitionCN: 科学实验或临床试验的详细书面计划
senses.example: The trial protocol specifies doses, check-ups and stopping rules.
senses.exampleCN: 试验方案规定了剂量、检查和终止规则。
senses.why: Science keeps the old 'draft, minutes' sense alive: before anything is done, the plan is written down on the first sheet. A protocol is the document that tells the researcher what may be done.
senses.whyCN: 科学保留了古老的“草稿、记录”义：在做任何事之前，计划先被写在首页上。方案就是告诉研究者可以做什么的那份文件。

senses.title: Rules between machines: the computer protocol
senses.titleCN: 计算机协议：机器之间的外交礼节
senses.definition: a set of rules governing how data is exchanged between computers or devices
senses.definitionCN: 规定计算机或设备之间如何交换数据的规则集合
senses.example: HTTP is the protocol your browser uses to fetch a web page.
senses.exampleCN: HTTP 是浏览器抓取网页时使用的协议。
senses.why: Computers need the same thing diplomats need: an agreed order for who speaks first and how a message is acknowledged. The 20c technical sense borrows the word for rules of exchange.
senses.whyCN: 计算机需要的东西与外交官相同：约定谁先发言、消息如何确认的次序。20 世纪的技术义借用了这个表示“交换规则”的词。

senses.title: The first sheet: original draft and minutes
senses.titleCN: 原始记录、草案：贴在卷首的那张纸
senses.definition: the original draft of a document, or the minutes of a transaction (now obsolete)
senses.definitionCN: 文件的原始草稿，或交易的会议记录（现已废弃）
senses.example: The clerk kept the protocol of the negotiations in a leather ledger.
senses.exampleCN: 书记员把谈判的原始记录保存在一本皮面账册里。
senses.why: Greek prōtokollon literally meant 'first sheet glued onto a manuscript', where the contents were listed. English took it in the 1540s as the draft or minutes — the literal sheet before the finished text.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 prōtokollon 字面就是“贴在文稿上的第一张纸”，上面列着目录。英语在 16 世纪 40 年代借入时指草稿或会议记录——成文之前的那张实指纸片。

senses.title: The standard treatment plan
senses.titleCN: 治疗方案：医院里的标准流程
senses.definition: a standard plan for treating a particular illness or condition
senses.definitionCN: 治疗某种疾病或状况的标准方案
senses.example: Patients on the new protocol showed fewer side effects.
senses.exampleCN: 采用新治疗方案的患者副作用更少。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the research-protocol sense and applied it to care: a fixed sequence of tests and drugs that every patient on the plan receives.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了研究方案的义项，并把它用到治疗上：一套固定的检查与用药顺序，凡进入该方案的患者都照此接受。

senses.title: The diplomatic instrument
senses.titleCN: 外交文书：正式归档的那份文件
senses.definition: a formal diplomatic document, especially one recording an agreement or understanding
senses.definitionCN: 正式的外交文件，尤指记录某项协议或谅解的文件
senses.example: The protocol was deposited with the foreign ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 这份议定书已交存外交部。
senses.why: In 19c diplomacy, protocol named the document signed by friendly powers to secure certain ends by peaceful means. It is the treaty sense given a formal, archival body.
senses.whyCN: 在 19 世纪外交中，protocol 指友好国家为以和平方式实现某些目标而签署的文件。它是条约义项获得了正式、可归档的形体。

senses.title: Precedence at a state occasion
senses.titleCN: 礼宾次序：国事场合的座次表
senses.definition: the order of precedence and ceremony observed on formal state or institutional occasions
senses.definitionCN: 正式国事或机构场合所遵循的位次与仪式次序
senses.example: Seating followed strict protocol, with the dean at the head of the table.
senses.exampleCN: 座次遵循严格的礼宾次序，院长坐在长桌首位。
senses.why: The etiquette sense widened from diplomacy to any formal hierarchy. Who walks in first, who sits where — the old first sheet still dictates the order of the room.
senses.whyCN: 礼仪义从外交扩展到任何正式等级场合。谁先入场、谁坐哪里——那张古老的首张贴纸仍在规定房间里的次序。

intro.en: Protocol begins as bookbinding: a sheet of contents glued to the front of a manuscript. From that 'first sheet' come the draft, the official record, the treaty, the etiquette of diplomats, the plan of an experiment, and finally the rules that let computers talk.
intro.cn: protocol 起于书籍装订：一张目录纸贴在文稿卷首。从这张“首张贴纸”衍生出草稿、官方记录、条约、外交礼节、实验方案，最后是让计算机彼此交谈的规则。

items.en: Prōtokollon meant 'first sheet glued onto a manuscript', from prōtos 'first' plus kolla 'glue'. The origin of kolla itself is uncertain, so that element is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: prōtokollon 意为“贴在文稿上的第一张纸”，由 prōtos“第一”加 kolla“胶水”构成。kolla 本身的来源不确定，因此这一成分标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Protocollum meant 'draft', literally 'the first sheet of a volume', on which contents and errata were written. The physical sheet becomes a textual record.
items.cn: protocollum 意为“草稿”，字面是“一卷书的第一张纸”，上面写着目录和勘误。实指的纸片变成了文本记录。

items.en: Prothocole passed into French, where the sense developed from 'rough draft; original copy of a treaty' to 'official record of a transaction' to 'diplomatic document'.
items.cn: prothocole 传入法语，词义从“粗略草稿、条约原件”发展为“交易的官方记录”，再发展为“外交文件”。

items.en: English first records prothogol 'prologue' (mid-15c.), then prothogall 'draft of a document, minutes of a transaction, original of any writing' (1540s). These senses are now obsolete.
items.cn: 英语最早记录 prothogol“序言”（15 世纪中），随后记录 prothogall“文件草稿、交易记录、任何文书的原件”（16 世纪 40 年代）。这些义项今已废弃。

items.en: 'Diplomatic document signed by friendly powers' develops through the 17c.–19c.; the French sense 'formula of diplomatic etiquette' is attested in English by 1896.
items.cn: “友好国家签署的外交文件”一义在 17 至 19 世纪发展起来；法语“外交礼仪程式”这一义项于 1896 年在英语中出现。

items.en: 'Conventional proper conduct' is recorded from 1952. The technical sense 'rules for exchanging data between computers' arose in the 20c. as engineers borrowed the idea of an agreed order of exchange.
items.cn: “约定俗成的得体举止”记录于 1952 年。技术义“计算机之间交换数据的规则”在 20 世纪出现，工程师们借用了“约定的交换次序”这一观念。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the proto- opening but differs in the second element; the meaning group shares the idea of rules or formal agreement, not the shape.
note.cn: 形近组共享 proto- 开头，但第二成分不同；近义组共享“规则或正式约定”的概念，而非外形。

entries.definition: a first model from which later versions are developed. It shares proto- 'first' but ends in -type, not -col.
entries.definitionCN: 原型；最初模型。它共享 proto-“第一”，但词尾是 -type，不是 -col。

entries.definition: a hypothetical first cell. It looks like protocol but its second element is 'cell'.
entries.definitionCN: 原始细胞（假想中的最初细胞）。它形似 protocol，但第二成分是“细胞”。

entries.definition: a positively charged particle in the nucleus. The word means 'the first one', with no 'glue' element.
entries.definitionCN: 质子。这个词意为“第一个”，没有“胶水”这一成分。

entries.definition: the opening of a play or book. It also means 'first speech', but from logos rather than kolla.
entries.definitionCN: 序言；开场白。它也指“最先的话”，但来自 logos 而非 kolla。

entries.definition: an arrangement people accept. It is broader and less formal than a protocol.
entries.definitionCN: 协议；一致意见。它比 protocol 更宽泛、更不正式。

entries.definition: the conventional rules of polite behavior. It matches protocol's ceremonial sense.
entries.definitionCN: 礼节；礼仪。它对应 protocol 的仪式义。

entries.definition: an established way of doing something. It matches protocol as an operating sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 程序；步骤。它对应 protocol 作为操作流程的义项。

entries.definition: a widely accepted custom or practice. It is unwritten where protocol is often written.
entries.definitionCN: 惯例；公约。它常是不成文的，而 protocol 常是成文的。

entries.definition: a formal written agreement between states. It is the legal core of protocol sense 01.
entries.definitionCN: 条约。它是 protocol 第 1 义项的法律核心。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Greek kolla 'glue', prōtokollon 'first sheet', and the modern protocol stack that keeps machines in order.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：希腊语 kolla“胶水”、prōtokollon“首张贴纸”，以及让机器守秩序的现代协议栈。

normal.en: proto- 'first' + kollon 'glue': the first sheet glued to the scroll — protocol.
normal.cn: proto-“第一”+ kollon“胶水”：贴在卷首的第一张纸——protocol。

normal.en: The first sheet listed contents, so protocol came to mean the plan and the record.
normal.cn: 首张贴纸列着目录，所以 protocol 后来既指方案也指记录。

normal.en: Diplomatic protocol is a treaty's first page turned into behaviour.
normal.cn: 外交礼节就是条约的第一页变成了行为举止。

normal.en: A lab protocol is the first sheet of an experiment, written before anyone starts.
normal.cn: 实验室方案就是实验的首张贴纸，在任何人动手之前写好。

normal.en: A network protocol is etiquette for machines: who speaks, in what order, and how to reply.
normal.cn: 网络协议就是机器的礼节：谁先说、按什么次序、如何回应。

abstract.en: One idea runs through all senses: an agreed order written at the front and then obeyed.
abstract.cn: 一个观念贯穿所有义项：写在最前面、随后被遵守的约定次序。

abstract.en: The word moves from paper to people to machines without changing its logic.
abstract.cn: 这个词从纸面走到人，再走到机器，逻辑始终没变。

abstract.en: Protocol is the price of cooperation: someone must go first, and everyone must know it.
abstract.cn: 协议是合作的代价：总得有人先来，而所有人都得知道这一点。

examples.en: The Kyoto Protocol set binding targets for greenhouse gases.
examples.cn: 《京都议定书》为温室气体设定了有约束力的目标。

examples.en: Nurses check the protocol before administering a new drug.
examples.cn: 护士在给新药之前会核对规程。

examples.en: The two networks could not talk because they used different protocols.
examples.cn: 这两个网络因使用不同的协议而无法通信。

dict_mnemonic.text: proto（第一）+ col（胶水）——贴在卷首的第一张纸，写着规矩；谐音“普罗托科尔”：先（pro）把规矩贴在开头，大家照做 → protocol 协议；礼仪

root: 源自希腊语 prōtokollon“贴在文稿卷首的第一张纸”，由 prōtos“第一”加 kolla“胶水”构成，经中世纪拉丁语 protocollum 与古法语进入英语；核心是“写在前头、必须遵守的次序”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses built on one physical thing: the first sheet glued to a document. That sheet held the contents and the order, so protocol became draft, record, treaty, etiquette, procedure, experiment plan, treatment plan, and the rules by which computers exchange data.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都建筑在同一个实物上：贴在文件卷首的第一张纸。那张纸写着目录与次序，于是 protocol 依次成为草稿、记录、条约、礼节、规程、实验方案、治疗方案，以及计算机交换数据的规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first sheet glued to the front of a scroll, listing the order of what follows.
core.cn: 核心意象：贴在卷首的第一张纸，列明后续内容的次序。

branches.en: THE DOCUMENT: the original draft and minutes, and the formal agreement they grow into.
branches.cn: 文书：原始草稿与会议记录，以及由此长成的正式协议。

branches.en: THE ORDER OF PEOPLE: diplomatic etiquette and the precedence observed at state occasions.
branches.cn: 人的次序：外交礼节，以及国事场合遵循的位次。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN PLAN: operating procedures, experiment protocols and standard treatment plans.
branches.cn: 书面方案：操作规程、实验方案与标准治疗方案。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: the formal diplomatic document deposited with a ministry.
branches.cn: 正式文书：交存外交部的正式外交文件。

branches.en: THE RULES OF EXCHANGE: the protocol that lets machines speak to one another.
branches.cn: 交换规则：让机器彼此交谈的协议。

intro.en: Protocol is proto- plus koll- plus -on. Its family shows the Greek prefix prōto- 'first' and the glue-root kolla, which also reaches English through collage and collagen.
intro.cn: protocol 是 proto- 加 koll- 再加 -on。它的词族展示希腊前缀 prōto-“第一”与“胶水”词根 kolla，后者也通过 collage、collagen 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Greek prōtos 'first' yields the combining form proto-; Greek kolla 'glue' is the base of protocol, collage and collagen, though the deeper origin of kolla is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 prōtos“第一”给出构词成分 proto-；希腊语 kolla“胶水”是 protocol、collage、collagen 的基础，不过 kolla 更深层的来源不确定。

items.meaning: the first sheet glued on; rules and records
items.meaningCN: 协议；礼仪；规程（首张贴纸）
items.example: The hospital follows a strict protocol for infection control.
items.exampleCN: 这家医院遵循严格的感染控制规程。

items.example: The team built a prototype before mass production.
items.exampleCN: 团队在大规模生产之前造了一个原型。

items.meaning: the first actor; the leading character
items.example: The protagonist narrates the whole novel.

items.exampleCN: 原生动物生活在池水中。

items.meaningCN: 质子（核中的“第一个”粒子）
items.example: A proton carries a positive charge.

items.meaning: the original living substance of a cell
items.meaningCN: 原生质（细胞的原初生命物质）
items.example: Early biologists studied the protoplasm of cells.
items.exampleCN: 早期生物学家研究细胞的原生质。

items.meaning: the period just before written history
items.meaningCN: 原史时期（有文字记载之前的那一段）
items.example: Protohistory covers cultures that left no writing.
items.exampleCN: 原史时期涵盖没有留下文字的文化。

items.meaning: a picture made by gluing pieces together
items.meaningCN: 拼贴画（把碎片粘在一起）
items.example: The artist made a collage from old photographs.
items.exampleCN: 这位艺术家用旧照片做了一幅拼贴画。

items.meaning: the protein that 'produces glue' in skin and bone

definition_zh: 自豪地；骄傲地；傲慢地
definition_en: in a way that shows pleasure and satisfaction in what one has done, in a way that shows too high an opinion of oneself, or in a way that stands out boldly
core_image: 一个人挺直背站在人群前面，下巴微微抬起，眼睛发亮
scene: 女儿把奖状举到胸前，母亲站在旁边，背挺得笔直，见人就说这是孩子自己挣来的。The mother spoke proudly of her daughter's first prize.
sceneCN: 这里表示「自豪地」（第 1 个义项：因成绩或亲人而心里发亮）；句意为母亲一说起女儿得的一等奖，语气里全是自豪。

pos.zh: 自豪地；骄傲地；傲慢地

derivatives.zh: 本词的基础形容词，加上 -ly 即构成 proudly，义为「自豪的；骄傲的」
同族名词，与 proud 同出一源，义为「自豪；骄傲；自尊」
由 pride 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「骄傲的；自视过高的」

senses.title: In a way that shows pleasure in an achievement
senses.definition: in a way that shows you feel pleased and satisfied about something you or people close to you have done
senses.definitionCN: 表现出对自己或亲近之人所做成的事感到满意、心里发亮
senses.example: She proudly showed us the letter her son had written.
senses.exampleCN: 她自豪地把儿子写的信拿给我们看。
senses.why: Proud first described a person of worth and standing, and -ly turns that standing into a manner, so proudly is how someone carries a good result.
senses.whyCN: proud 最初形容一个人有分量、站得住，-ly 把这种站位变成举止方式，所以 proudly 就是一个人带着好成绩走路的样子。

senses.title: In a way that shows too high an opinion of oneself
senses.definition: in a way that shows you believe you are better than the people around you
senses.definitionCN: 表现出自认比周围的人高一等
senses.example: He proudly refused the advice of every older worker.
senses.exampleCN: 他傲慢地拒绝了每一位老工人的劝告。
senses.why: The same high standing can be earned or merely assumed, and when nothing was earned the manner turns into arrogance, so the adverb carries both praise and blame.
senses.whyCN: 同样一种「站得高」，可以是挣来的，也可以是自己假定的；当它并非挣来，这种举止就变成傲慢，所以这个副词既带称赞也带责备。

senses.title: In a way that rises or stands out boldly
senses.definition: used of a building, a ship or a feature that rises or shows itself in a bold, dignified way
senses.definitionCN: 用于建筑、船只或某处特征，指其挺拔、醒目而体面地立在那里
senses.example: The old tower stands proudly above the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧塔傲然立在港湾之上。
senses.why: English lends the human posture to things: whatever rises straight and refuses to hide seems to hold its head up, so a tower can stand proudly.
senses.whyCN: 英语把人的姿态借给了物：凡是笔直立起、又不肯躲藏的，就像抬着头一样，于是塔也能 stand proudly。

intro.en: Proudly is an English-made adverb from proud, a word that came through French and is generally traced to a Late Latin sense of being useful or of value.
intro.cn: proudly 是英语内部由 proud 加 -ly 造出的副词；proud 经法语而来，一般认为可追到晚期拉丁语中「有用、有价值」的意思。

items.en: The Latin verb prodesse meant to be useful or to do good, and a thing that is useful can be counted as worth something.
items.cn: 拉丁动词 prodesse 意为有用、带来好处；有用的东西自然被视为有价值。

items.en: The adjective prode meant useful, profitable or brave, and it is generally cited as the starting point of the French word.
items.cn: 形容词 prode 意为有用的、有利的、勇敢的，一般认为这是法语那个词的起点。

items.en: Old French prou or prud described someone brave, worthy and of good standing.
items.cn: 古法语 prou 或 prud 形容一个人勇敢、可敬、有地位。

items.en: Middle English proud could mean brave and magnificent as well as having a high opinion of oneself.
items.cn: 中古英语 proud 既能表示勇敢、气派，也能表示自视甚高。

items.en: Modern English keeps both sides, so proud is praise in a parent's mouth and blame in a critic's, and -ly turns each into a manner.
items.cn: 现代英语把两面都留下：在父母嘴里 proud 是称赞，在批评者嘴里是责备，而 -ly 把这两种都变成举止方式。

note.en: The first group is the small family of pride words, including one that only looks alike; the second group gathers adverbs for feeling good about oneself.
note.cn: 第一组是与「自豪」有关的小词族，其中一个只是看起来像；第二组收表示「对自己感觉良好」的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective behind the adverb: feeling pleased, or thinking too well of oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 本词所依附的形容词：感到自豪，或自视过高。

entries.definition: The noun for that feeling; it also names a group of lions.
entries.definitionCN: 这种感觉的名词；也指一群狮子。

entries.definition: To push with a finger or a stick; only the spelling is close, the origin is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 用手指或棍子戳；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: In a way that shows you think you are better than others.
entries.definitionCN: 表现出自认高人一等。

entries.definition: In a cold and superior manner.
entries.definitionCN: 冷漠而居高临下地。

entries.definition: In a way that shows belief in oneself or in one's judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 表现出对自己或自己的判断有信心。

entries.definition: In an impressive and self-important manner.
entries.definitionCN: 气派十足、颇为自得地。

normalIntro.en: The adverb adds a manner to a word about standing tall: whoever is proud holds the body, and the voice, a little higher than usual.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词给「站得高」这个词添上了举止：心里自豪的人，身体和声音都会比平常抬高一点。

normal.en: Proudly is simply proud plus -ly, so the adverb is the adjective's posture turned into a way of speaking or standing.
normal.cn: proudly 就是 proud 加 -ly，所以这个副词是形容词的姿态变成了说话或站立的方式。

normal.en: Pride is the noun of the same feeling; the pair pride and proud is irregular in shape but regular in meaning.
normal.cn: pride 是同一份感觉的名词；pride 与 proud 形式不整齐，意思却一一对应。

normal.en: The old sense of proud as brave explains why a tower or a ship can stand proudly: that is height, not vanity.
normal.cn: proud 古有「勇敢、气派」之义，这解释了塔或船为何能 stand proudly：那是高度，不是虚荣。

normal.en: A parent's proudly and a critic's proudly sound the same, and only the situation tells praise from blame.
normal.cn: 父母嘴里的 proudly 与批评者嘴里的 proudly 发音相同，只有情境能分出称赞与责备。

normal.en: The -ly ending is native English, so proudly was built inside the language from an adjective borrowed through French.
normal.cn: -ly 是英语本族词尾，所以 proudly 是用一个经法语借来的形容词在英语内部造出来的。

abstract.en: Pride lifts the body, and the adverb records that lift in the shoulders and in the voice.
abstract.cn: 自豪会把身体抬起，这个副词记录的就是肩膀与声音里的那一下抬起。

abstract.en: One manner serves both self-respect and vanity because the outside looks the same, and only the inside differs.
abstract.cn: 同一种举止既用于自尊也用于虚荣，因为外表一样，差别只在里面。

abstract.en: To speak proudly is to let others see how much a thing matters to you, which is a small act of exposure.
abstract.cn: 自豪地说，就是让别人看见某件事对你有多重要，这是一种小小的袒露。

examples.en: She proudly introduced her father to the class.
examples.cn: 她自豪地把父亲介绍给全班。

examples.en: The team proudly displayed the trophy in the hall.
examples.cn: 球队把奖杯自豪地摆在大厅里。

examples.en: He proudly ignored the warnings of his friends.
examples.cn: 他傲慢地不理会朋友们的提醒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑劳德利」——胸脯一挺，声音就跟着亮起来；记住 proudly 是自豪地、骄傲地。

root: proudly 由形容词 proud 加副词后缀 -ly 构成。proud 经古法语 prou、prud 进入英语，一般认为更早可追到晚期拉丁语 prode（有用的、有价值的），再往前是 prodesse（有益）。所以这个词的起点不是「骄傲」，而是「有分量、有价值」。英语里 pride 是同一族的名词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a body held higher than usual; the senses divide into earned satisfaction, unearned superiority, and the borrowed posture of tall things.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「比平常抬得更高的身体」；义项由此分出挣来的满足、没挣来的优越，以及借给高耸之物的那种姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing straight with the chin slightly raised and the eyes bright.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人挺直站着，下巴微微抬起，眼睛发亮。

branches.en: a prize held against the chest
branches.cn: 奖状贴在胸前

branches.en: a chin raised at advice that is refused
branches.cn: 拒绝劝告时抬起的下巴

branches.en: a tower above the harbour
branches.cn: 港湾上方的一座塔

branches.en: height that is earned and height that is only built
branches.cn: 挣来的高度与只是造出来的高度

branches.en: one posture for pride and for stone
branches.cn: 一种姿态，既属于骄傲也属于石头

intro.en: A Late Latin adjective of worth, its French descendant, and the native English -ly that turns an adjective into a manner hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示「有价值」的晚期拉丁语形容词、它在法语里的后身，以及把形容词变成举止的英语本族词尾 -ly，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Prode and prodesse are the Latin forms usually cited, while the French stage of the journey is the part that is certain.
latinIntro.cn: prode 与 prodesse 是通常引用的拉丁语形式；可以确定的是它经法语传来的那一段。

items.meaning: to be useful, to do good
having a high opinion of oneself

latinEntries.meaning: to be useful, to do good

definition_zh: 证明；证实；结果是；检验；证明自己
definition_en: to show that something is true by evidence, to turn out to be a particular way, or to test something in practice
core_image: 一叠材料被推到桌上，最后一页的印章让所有疑问停了下来
scene: 争论一直持续到深夜，直到有人把当年的登记簿翻到那一页，指着上面的签名。The old register proved that the land had belonged to her family.
sceneCN: 这里表示「证明、证实」（第 1 个义项：用证据使某件事确定为真）；句意为那本旧登记簿证明了这块地一直属于她家。

pos.zh: 证明；证实；结果是；检验

derivatives.zh: 与 prove 同源的名词，经古法语 preove 而来，义为「证据；证明」
由过去分词转成的形容词，义为「已被证实的；经考验的」
由 prove 加 -able 构成，义为「可证明的」
由 prove 加否定前缀 dis- 构成，义为「证明……有误；驳倒」

senses.title: To show that something is true
senses.definition: to give facts, documents or tests that make it certain that something is true or real
senses.definitionCN: 拿出事实、文件或检验，使某事被确定为真或确实存在
senses.example: The fingerprints proved that he had been in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 指纹证明他曾在那间屋子里。
senses.why: Latin probare meant to test something and find it good, so proving starts as an examination that ends in a verdict rather than as a mere opinion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 probare 意为检验某物并认定它站得住，所以「证明」起初是一场检验，最后落成判决，而不只是看法。

senses.title: To turn out to be a particular thing
senses.definition: to be found, after events have unfolded, to have a certain quality, often one that was not expected
senses.definitionCN: 事情展开之后，被发现具有某种性质，且常是原先没料到的
senses.example: The shortcut proved longer than the road we usually take.
senses.exampleCN: 那条近路结果比我们常走的路还远。
senses.why: Once a test is finished, the result simply is what it is; English lets the verb carry that outcome, so a thing can prove difficult without anyone proving it.
senses.whyCN: 检验结束之后，结果就摆在那里；英语让这个动词直接承担结果，于是事物本身可以 prove difficult，而不需要谁去证明它。

senses.title: To test something in order to learn its quality
senses.definition: to try a method, a weapon or a machine under real conditions to see whether it works
senses.definitionCN: 在真实条件下试用某种方法、武器或机器，看它是否管用
senses.example: The engineers proved the new pump under heavy load before selling it.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在重载下检验了新水泵，然后才出售。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer made visible: before a thing can be proved true, it has to be put to the test, and the verb still names that trial.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老那层意思的直接显现：在被证明为真之前，东西得先经受检验，而这个动词至今仍指那场试验。

senses.title: To show one's own ability or courage
senses.definition: to show through action that one deserves a place, a role or respect
senses.definitionCN: 通过行动表明自己配得上某个位置、角色或尊重
senses.example: She proved herself in her first month on the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 她在上夜班的第一个月就证明了自己。
senses.why: When the thing being proved is the speaker, the test and the result collapse into one act, which is why English says prove oneself rather than adding true as well.
senses.whyCN: 当被证明的对象是说话者本人时，检验与结果合成一个动作，所以英语说 prove oneself，不再额外加 true。

intro.en: Prove descends from a Latin verb that meant to test and to judge as good; English keeps both the trial and the verdict, and later let the word also mean to turn out.
intro.cn: prove 源自一个意为「检验并判定为好」的拉丁动词；英语同时保留了检验与判决，后来又让它表示「结果如何」。

items.en: Probus meant upright, honest and of good quality, said of a person or a thing that had been checked.
items.cn: probus 意为正直、诚实、品质良好，用于经过查验的人或物。

items.en: Probare meant to test something and to approve it as good, joining the act of examining to the verdict.
items.cn: probare 意为检验某物并认可它合格，把查验的动作与判决连在一起。

items.en: The participle probatus described what had stood the test, and it is the shape behind the English word.
items.cn: 分词 probatus 描述经住了检验的东西，是英语这个词背后的形式。

items.en: Old French prover meant to test and to demonstrate, and it brought the verb into English.
items.cn: 古法语 prover 意为检验、论证，把这个动词带进英语。

items.en: English split the old family: proof became the noun for the evidence, while prove kept the testing and added the modern sense of turning out.
items.cn: 英语把这一族拆开：proof 成为表示证据的名词，prove 留住检验，又添上「结果是」这层现代用法。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb of testing, including the noun English split off from it; the second group gathers verbs for showing something to be true or false.
note.cn: 第一组共用表示「检验」的拉丁动词，包括英语从它分出去的名词；第二组收表示「表明真假」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for evidence that settles a question, split off from the same French form.
entries.definitionCN: 能定下疑问的证据名词，与动词同出法语形式。

entries.definition: The participle used as an adjective for something already shown to be true.
entries.definitionCN: 分词转作形容词，指已被证实的东西。

entries.definition: Likely to be true, from the same Latin verb of testing and approving.
entries.definitionCN: 很可能是真的，出自同一个表示检验与认可的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: To investigate closely, originally to test a wound or a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细查究，原指探查伤口或表面。

entries.definition: To show clearly by argument or by an example.
entries.definitionCN: 用论证或实例清楚地表明。

entries.definition: To check that something is true or accurate.
entries.definitionCN: 核查某事是否真实、准确。

entries.definition: To show that a fact is certain, often in a formal way.
entries.definitionCN: 表明某事实确凿，常较正式。

entries.definition: To be discovered to be a particular way in the end.
entries.definitionCN: 最终被发现是某种样子。

normalIntro.en: The family keeps the picture of a test that ends in a verdict: something is put under pressure, and the result is then allowed to speak.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词保留着「检验之后落成判决」的画面：某物被压上压力，然后让结果自己说话。

normal.en: Probare is to test and to approve, so prove carries a courtroom inside it: first the examination, then the finding.
normal.cn: probare 既是检验也是认可，所以 prove 里装着一间法庭：先审，再判。

normal.en: Proof is the same family seen as a thing rather than an act, which is why a proof is handed over while a prove is performed.
normal.cn: proof 是同一族词被看成「物」而不是「动作」，所以 proof 可以递过去，prove 只能被执行。

normal.en: Probable keeps the approving half: what is probable has enough testing behind it to be believed.
normal.cn: probable 保留了「认可」的那一半：很可能的事，背后已有足够的检验让人相信。

normal.en: Disprove adds dis- to the front, so the test now ends in rejection instead of approval.
normal.cn: disprove 在前面加 dis-，于是检验以否定而不是认可收场。

normal.en: Prove looks like protect because both start with pro-, but probare means to test, and there is no covering anywhere in it.
normal.cn: prove 与 protect 都以 pro- 开头，但 probare 意为检验，其中没有任何「遮盖」。

abstract.en: A proof is a test that has stopped being a question, and the verb marks the moment that change happens.
abstract.cn: 证据是一场不再提问的检验，而这个动词标出的正是那变化发生的瞬间。

abstract.en: One word covers testing, judging and turning out because all three are stages of the same examination.
abstract.cn: 同一个词兼指检验、判定与结果，因为三者是同一场查验的不同阶段。

abstract.en: To prove something is to accept that it might fail, which is why the word is as much about risk as about certainty.
abstract.cn: 证明某物，就是承认它有可能失败，所以这个词既关乎确定，也关乎冒险。

examples.en: The video proved that the door had been locked all night.
examples.cn: 录像证明那扇门整夜都锁着。

examples.en: The task proved harder than anyone expected.
examples.cn: 这项任务结果比任何人预料的都难。

examples.en: He worked two extra shifts to prove himself.
examples.cn: 他多上了两个班来证明自己。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普如夫」——像「扑过去捋清楚」，把乱糟糟的事捋到只剩一条真相；记住 prove 是证明。

root: 拉丁语 probus（正直的、品质良好的）→ probare（检验、验后认可）→ probatus（经住检验的），经古法语 prover 进入英语；同族词还有 proof、probable、probe、probity。注意 prove 与 protect 都带前缀 pro-，但 prove 的词根是 probare（检验），protect 的词根是 tegere（覆盖），两者只是前缀相同。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a test ending in a verdict; the senses run from proving a fact, through the result of events, to testing a thing and proving oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「以检验收尾的判定」；义项从证明一个事实，到事情的结果，再到检验一物与证明自己。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of papers pushed across a table, and a stamp on the last page that ends every doubt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠材料被推到桌上，最后一页的印章让所有疑问停下来。

branches.en: a register opened to the page with the signature
branches.cn: 登记簿翻到有签名的那一页

branches.en: a short cut that turns out longer
branches.cn: 结果反而更远的那条近路

branches.en: a pump running under heavy load
branches.cn: 重载下运转的水泵

branches.en: a new worker taking the hardest shift
branches.cn: 新人接下最难的班次

branches.en: one word for examining and for concluding
branches.cn: 同一个词既指查验也指结论

intro.en: A Latin adjective of good quality, the verb of testing built on it, and the French and English forms that split into proof and prove hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示品质良好的拉丁形容词、由它构成的「检验」动词，以及分化为 proof 与 prove 的法语、英语形式，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Probus, probare and probatus are the reliable Latin cognates, and proof is the same family seen as a noun.
latinIntro.cn: probus、probare 与 probatus 是可靠的同源词；proof 则是同一族词被看成名词的样子。

definition_zh: 提供；供给；规定；供养；防备
definition_en: to give or supply something that is needed, to state a rule in a law or contract, or to support someone with money
core_image: 旅人站上高坡，把前路看得很远，再转身把干粮和水递给身后的人
scene: 洪水退去后的第三天，村口的空地上支起几张长桌，志愿者把水和面包摆成一排。The relief team came to provide blankets and hot food for the flooded villages.
sceneCN: 这里取「提供、供给」的意思（第 1 个义项：把别人需要的东西给出去）；句意为救援队来为受淹的村庄提供毛毯和热食。村口长桌上摆开的水和面包就是线索。

pos.zh: 提供；供给；规定；供养；为…做准备

derivatives.zh: 由 provide 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「供应者；提供者」
由拉丁语名词 provisio（预见、照料）经法语进入英语，义为「供应；条款；储备」
由拉丁词干 provid- 加 -ent 构成，义为「有远见的；用钱谨慎的」
由过去分词转成的连词，义为「假如；只要」，常见于 provided that

senses.title: To supply something that is needed
senses.definition: to give someone something they need or to make something available for use
senses.definitionCN: 把别人需要的东西给出去，或使某物可供使用
senses.example: The school provides free meals for children from poor families.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为贫困家庭的孩子提供免费餐食。
senses.why: Latin providere joins pro-, ahead, to videre, to see; seeing ahead means noticing a need before it arrives, and the next move is to get the thing ready and hand it over.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 providere 把表示「在前」的 pro- 接在 videre（看）上：提前看见，就是在需求到来之前先察觉；察觉之后最自然的动作，就是把东西备好递过去，于是「预先看见」变成了「供给」。

senses.title: To state as a rule in a law or contract
senses.definition: to establish a rule or condition in a law, contract or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 在法律、合同或协议中确立某条规则或条件
senses.example: The contract provides that the rent must be paid on the first day of each month.
senses.exampleCN: 合同规定租金须在每月第一天支付。
senses.why: A rule written in advance is itself a kind of foresight: the text settles now what will happen later, so the verb that means to get ready also names what a document lays down beforehand.
senses.whyCN: 提前写好的条文本身就是一种预见：文本在此刻就决定了以后会发生什么，所以那个表示「预先备好」的动词，也用来指文件事先订下的内容。

senses.title: To support someone financially
senses.definition: to earn the money that allows another person, especially a family member, to live
senses.definitionCN: 挣钱供另一个人生活，尤指供养家庭成员
senses.example: He works two jobs to provide for his elderly parents.
senses.exampleCN: 他打两份工来赡养年迈的父母。
senses.why: Providing for someone is looking ahead on their behalf: the money is set aside before the need is felt, which is the household version of seeing ahead.
senses.whyCN: 供养一个人，就是替对方往前看：钱在需求出现之前就留出来，这正是「预先看见」在家庭里的样子。

senses.title: To make preparation against something
senses.definition: to take action in advance so that a possible problem or danger does less harm
senses.definitionCN: 提前采取行动，使可能出现的问题或危险危害更小
senses.example: They built the wall to provide against flooding in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们修了这道墙，用来防备春季洪水。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is pure foresight with nothing given away: to provide against a risk is to see it coming and move before it lands.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层就是纯粹的「预先看见」，与给东西无关：provide against 某个风险，就是看出它会来，并在它落地之前先动手。

intro.en: Provide is built from two Latin pieces meaning ahead and to see, and that single image of foresight later spreads into supply, legal rules and family support.
intro.cn: provide 由两个拉丁语成分构成，意思分别是「在前」和「看」；这一「预先看见」的画面后来扩展到供给、法律条文与养家。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and it supplied the visual core of a large family of Latin words.
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」，为一大族拉丁词提供了「看」这个核心。

items.en: Pro- meant ahead or in front, so providere meant to see ahead, to foresee and to take care of something in advance.
items.cn: pro- 表示「在前、预先」，所以 providere 意为往前看、预见，并提前照管某事。

items.en: The noun providentia named foresight and careful management, and it survives in the English words providence and provident.
items.cn: 名词 providentia 指远见与谨慎的照料，它留在英语的 providence 与 provident 里。

items.en: Old French pourveoir kept both halves of the meaning: to foresee a need and to supply what it calls for.
items.cn: 古法语 pourveoir 保留了两半意思：既预见需求，也提供需求所需的东西。

items.en: English fixed the spelling as provide and carried the word into law, where a document provides, and into the household, where a wage provides for a family.
items.cn: 英语把拼写固定为 provide，并把这个词带进法律——文件可以「规定」，也带进家庭——工资可以「养家」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin verb of seeing ahead; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for giving what is needed.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「预先看见」动词上的词；近义组收表示「给出所需之物」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for supplying something, and also a clause in a document.
entries.definitionCN: 表示供应之事的名字，也指文件中的条款。

entries.definition: Care or guidance that looks ahead, often attributed to a higher power.
entries.definitionCN: 为将来作准备的照管，常被归于更高的力量。

entries.definition: Careful about the future, especially with money.
entries.definitionCN: 为将来打算的，尤指用钱谨慎的。

entries.definition: A person or a company that supplies something.
entries.definitionCN: 提供某物的人或机构。

entries.definition: To give or sell what is needed over time.
entries.definitionCN: 持续提供或出售所需之物。

entries.definition: To provide furniture or whatever else is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 提供家具或所需之物。

entries.definition: To present something for someone to take.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西拿出来供人取用。

entries.definition: To supply with tools or skills for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的提供工具或技能。

normalIntro.en: The word starts with a look into the future, not with a gift, and its family keeps returning to foresight, readiness and the handover that follows.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的起点是往未来看一眼，而不是送礼；同族词反复回到预见、准备以及随之而来的交付。

normal.en: Pro- means ahead and videre means to see, so provide begins with a look into the future rather than with an object.
normal.cn: pro- 意为「在前」，videre 意为「看」，所以 provide 的起点是往未来看一眼，而不是某件东西。

normal.en: Provision is the noun built on the same stem: what has been seen ahead and therefore got ready.
normal.cn: provision 是同一词干上的名词：预先看见、因此备好的东西。

normal.en: The legal use, as in the law provides, works because a written rule also decides the future in advance.
normal.cn: 法律用法如 the law provides 之所以成立，是因为写下的规则同样在提前决定未来。

normal.en: Provider adds -er, the person who does the providing, exactly as in employer and adviser.
normal.cn: provider 加 -er，指做「提供」这件事的人，与 employer、adviser 的构造相同。

normal.en: Provided that keeps the past participle and turns it into a condition: if this is seen to, the rest follows.
normal.cn: provided that 保留过去分词形式，把它变成条件：只要这一点被照看到，其余便随之成立。

abstract.en: To provide is to act on a future you have already seen, which is why the word sounds like care more than charity.
abstract.cn: 提供是对一个你已经看见的未来采取行动，所以这个词听起来更像照料，而不像施舍。

abstract.en: A law that provides and a parent who provides are doing one thing: fixing tomorrow before it arrives.
abstract.cn: 法律规定与父母供养做的是同一件事：在明天到来之前就把它安排下来。

abstract.en: The whole word lives in the gap between seeing a need and meeting it.
abstract.cn: 从看见需求到满足需求之间的那段距离，正是这个词的全部所在。

examples.en: The school provides free meals for children from poor families.
examples.cn: 学校为贫困家庭的孩子提供免费餐食。

examples.en: The contract provides that the rent must be paid on the first day of each month.
examples.cn: 合同规定租金须在每月第一天支付。

examples.en: He works two jobs to provide for his elderly parents.
examples.cn: 他打两份工来赡养年迈的父母。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑若外德」——听着像「铺好喂的」，先把吃的用的铺好喂到人跟前，正是提供。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（在前、预先）+ videre（看见）构成 providere，本义「预先看到、提前照管」，由此引申为「预备、供给、规定、供养」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is foresight; the senses divide into supplying a need, writing a rule down, supporting a family, and guarding against a risk.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「预先看见」；义项分成满足需求、把规则写下来、供养家人，以及防备风险。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveller standing on a rise, looking far down the road, then turning back to hand food and water to those behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：旅人站上高坡，把前路看得很远，然后转身把干粮和水递给身后的人。

branches.en: a table of food laid out before anyone asks
branches.cn: 没人开口前就摆好的一桌食物

branches.en: a clause printed in small type at the end of a contract
branches.cn: 合同末尾用小字印出的条款

branches.en: a wage that keeps an old couple fed
branches.cn: 让一对老人吃得上饭的一份工资

branches.en: a wall raised before the river rises
branches.cn: 河水上涨之前就砌起的墙

branches.en: a store of grain kept for a bad year
branches.cn: 为荒年留下的存粮

intro.en: A Latin prefix of forward movement and a Latin verb of seeing hold the word together, and French reshaped the verb before English took it.
intro.cn: 表示向前的拉丁语前缀与表示「看见」的拉丁语动词共同支撑这个词，法语先在中间改造了动词形式，英语随后借入。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre, to see, the compound providere, to see ahead, and the noun providentia, foresight, are the direct sources of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre（看见）、复合形式 providere（往前看）与名词 providentia（远见）是英语这个词的直接来源。

latinEntries.meaning: to see ahead, to take care

definition_zh: 省；行政区；领域；本分；外省
definition_en: a large administrative region of a country, or the area of activity and responsibility that belongs to someone
core_image: 一张地图被笔直的边界线切成几大块，每一块都有自己的名字和衙署
scene: 办公室的墙上挂着一张全国地图，有人用手指沿着边界线划出一大块，又在旁边写下自己的职责范围。The new railway will run through three provinces in the north.
sceneCN: 这里取「省、行政区」的意思（第 1 个义项：国家划分出的大行政区）；句意为这条新铁路将穿过北方的三个省。地图上被边界线划出的那一大块就是线索。

pos.zh: 省；行政区；领域；本分；外省

collocations.zh: 在首都以外的地方；在地方上

derivatives.zh: 由 province 加 -ial 构成，义为「省的；地方的；眼界狭隘的」
由 provincial 加 -ism 构成，义为「地方观念；偏狭」
由 provincial 加 -ly 构成，义为「以地方的方式；带着地方气」

senses.title: A large administrative region of a country
senses.definition: a large area of a country with its own local government, smaller than the whole state
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家中设有本地政府的大区域，范围小于整个国家
senses.example: She was born in a farming province in the west.
senses.exampleCN: 她出生在西部一个以农业为主的省。
senses.why: Latin provincia first named a duty assigned to a Roman official and only later the territory attached to that duty, so the word begins as a job before it becomes a piece of land.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 provincia 最初指分配给罗马官员的一项职责，后来才指随这项职责而来的地盘；所以这个词先是一份差事，然后才是一片土地。

senses.title: An area of activity that belongs to someone
senses.definition: a subject, duty or area of activity that is properly someone's concern
senses.definitionCN: 某种学科、职责或活动范围，正当地属于某人负责
senses.example: Deciding the budget is the province of the committee, not of one member.
senses.exampleCN: 决定预算属于委员会的职权，而不是某一位委员的事。
senses.why: If a province is the territory that comes with an office, then any field that comes with a role can be called a province, and the word shifts from land to responsibility.
senses.whyCN: 既然 province 是随官职而来的地盘，那么随某个身份而来的任何范围都可以叫 province，词义便从土地转到职责。

senses.title: The parts of a country outside the capital
senses.definition: the regions of a country away from the capital, often treated as less central or less sophisticated
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家中远离首都的地区，常被视为不那么中心或不够时髦
senses.example: After ten years in the capital, he moved back to the provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 在首都待了十年之后，他搬回了外省。
senses.why: A capital is a province too, but once it becomes the seat of power the rest of the map is named as a plural mass, and the phrase in the provinces quietly carries a judgement about the centre.
senses.whyCN: 首都本身也是一个省，可一旦它成为权力所在，地图上其余部分就被当成一个复数整体来称呼；in the provinces 这个说法里，悄悄带着以中心自居的评判。

intro.en: Province comes from a Latin word for a duty laid on an official; where that Latin word itself comes from is still debated, and it is not related to the verb provide.
intro.cn: province 来自一个表示「交给官员的职责」的拉丁语词；这个拉丁词本身的来源至今仍有争论，它与动词 provide 并无同源关系。

items.en: Provincia named a charge, an office or a command given to a Roman magistrate, and then the territory that came with it; its own origin is uncertain, and a common guess links it to pro- plus vincere, to win.
items.cn: provincia 指交给罗马官员的任务、职位或兵权，后来也指随之而来的辖区；它自身的来源不确定，一般认为可能与 pro- 加 vincere（战胜）有关。

items.en: Under the empire the word settled on the governed lands outside Italy, each with a governor sent from Rome.
items.cn: 在帝国时期，这个词固定指意大利之外受管辖的土地，每一块都派有从罗马出去的总督。

items.en: Old French province kept both the administrative and the territorial senses and passed them on to English.
items.cn: 古法语 province 同时保留行政与地域两层意思，并把它们传给英语。

items.en: Middle English province named a church district as well as a region of the realm, so the word was already used for several kinds of division.
items.cn: 中古英语的 province 既指教会辖区，也指王国中的区域，所以这个词早已用于好几种划分。

items.en: Modern English keeps the political sense, adds the figurative sense of a field of knowledge, and uses the plural for everything outside the capital.
items.cn: 现代英语保留政治义，增加「知识领域」的比喻义，并用复数指首都以外的一切地方。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words built on or close to the Latin word for a province; the near-meaning group holds words for regions and fields of activity.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「行省」一词上或与其形近的词；近义组收表示区域与活动范围的词。

entries.definition: Relating to a province, or narrow in outlook.
entries.definitionCN: 与省有关的，或指眼界狭隘的。

entries.definition: Interest in one's own province, or a narrow local outlook.
entries.definitionCN: 对本地事务的关注，或狭隘的地方观念。

entries.definition: In a way that relates to a province or shows a narrow outlook.
entries.definitionCN: 以与省相关的方式，或带着地方偏狭地。

entries.definition: Foresight or care, from Latin providere; the spelling is close but the root differs.
entries.definitionCN: 远见与照管，来自拉丁语 providere；拼写相近，但词源不同。

entries.definition: A large area of a country or of the world.
entries.definitionCN: 国家或世界中的一大片区域。

entries.definition: An area marked off for administrative purposes.
entries.definitionCN: 为行政目的划出的区域。

entries.definition: A field of knowledge or activity under someone's control.
entries.definitionCN: 在某人掌控下的知识或活动领域。

entries.definition: A kingdom, or a sphere of activity.
entries.definitionCN: 王国，或某个活动范围。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as a duty given to an official and ends as a piece of the map, and its family keeps turning on what belongs to whom.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「交给官员的一份差事」开始，最后落在「地图上的一块」，同族词始终围绕「什么归谁管」。

normal.en: Provincia in Latin was a job given to an official, and the land came second, which is why the word can still mean a duty today.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 provincia 是交给官员的一项差事，土地是后来才附上的，所以这个词今天仍能表示职责。

normal.en: The word is not related to provide: one comes from provincia, the other from providere, and their only link is a shared opening syllable.
normal.cn: 这个词与 provide 无关：一个来自 provincia，一个来自 providere，两者唯一的联系只是开头音节相同。

normal.en: Provincial adds -ial to make the adjective, and it carries both the neutral sense of local and the unkind sense of narrow.
normal.cn: provincial 加 -ial 构成形容词，既中性地表示「地方的」，也带贬义地表示「眼界窄的」。

normal.en: The plural in the provinces turns a map into a judgement, since it is always said from the point of view of the capital.
normal.cn: the provinces 这个复数说法把地图变成了评判，因为它总是从首都的视角说出来的。

normal.en: A church province and a political province are both divisions under one authority, which is how a single Latin word came to cover both.
normal.cn: 教会省与政治省都是在同一权威之下的划分，一个拉丁词就这样同时覆盖了两者。

abstract.en: A province is a piece of the map drawn by someone in the centre, so the word always carries a viewpoint.
abstract.cn: 省是中心的人画在地图上的一个格子，所以这个词里始终带着一个视角。

abstract.en: Calling a field your province is a quiet claim that others should keep out of it.
abstract.cn: 把某个领域称作自己的 province，是在不动声色地要求别人不要插手。

abstract.en: Empires divide land into provinces and people divide knowledge the same way, which is why one word serves both.
abstract.cn: 帝国把土地分成行省，人也照样把知识分成领域，所以同一个词能管两件事。

examples.en: She was born in a farming province in the west.
examples.cn: 她出生在西部一个以农业为主的省。

examples.en: Deciding the budget is the province of the committee, not of one member.
examples.cn: 决定预算属于委员会的职权，而不是某一位委员的事。

examples.en: After ten years in the capital, he moved back to the provinces.
examples.cn: 在首都待了十年之后，他搬回了外省。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若文斯」——听着像「评文事」，地方上的文书杂事都归它管，一个省就是这样一个摊子。

root: 拉丁语 provincia（交给官员的职责及其辖区），自身来源不确定，一般认为或与 pro- 加 vincere（战胜）有关；经古法语 province 进入英语，与 provide、provision 不同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a division under one authority; the senses divide into the administrative region, the field that belongs to a role, and the whole country outside the capital.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「在同一权威之下划出的一块」；义项分成行政区、归属于某个身份的领域，以及首都以外的整个地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a map cut by straight boundary lines into large blocks, each with its own name and its own office.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张地图被笔直的边界线切成几大块，每一块都有自己的名字和衙署。

branches.en: a boundary line drawn across a map
branches.cn: 地图上画出的一条边界线

branches.en: a governor arriving at a distant seat of office
branches.cn: 总督抵达远处的治所

branches.en: a committee claiming a subject as its own
branches.cn: 把某个议题划归自己的委员会

branches.en: a train leaving the capital for smaller towns
branches.cn: 驶离首都开往小城镇的火车

branches.en: a field marked off like a province on paper
branches.cn: 像纸上行省一样被划出来的领域

intro.en: A Latin noun of assigned duty and its adjective hold the word together, while English endings turn the same stem into an adjective, a noun of attitude and an adverb.
intro.cn: 表示「分派职责」的拉丁语名词及其形容词共同支撑这个词，英语词尾又把同一词干变成形容词、表示态度的名词和副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin provincia, a charge or a governed territory, and the adjective provincialis, of a province, stand behind the English word and its relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 provincia（职责、辖地）与形容词 provincialis（省的）是英语这个词及其同族词的来源。

definition_zh: 条款；规定；供应；提供；储备；预备
definition_en: a condition written into a law or contract, the act of supplying something, or a store of supplies kept for future use
core_image: 仓库里一袋袋粮食靠墙码好，门边贴着一张写明分配办法的纸
scene: 出发去山区之前，队长把面粉和罐头清点了一遍，又把分配办法写在纸上贴到门边。The expedition carried enough provisions for two weeks in the mountains.
sceneCN: 这里取「储备、给养」的意思（第 3 个义项：为将来备下的物资）；句意为探险队带上了足够在山里用两周的给养。靠墙码好的粮食和罐头就是线索。

pos.zh: 条款；规定；供应；提供；储备；预备

collocations.phrase: under the provisions of the law

derivatives.zh: 与 provision 同出拉丁语 providere（预先看见），义为「提供；规定」
由 provision 加 -al 构成，义为「临时的；暂定的」
由 provisional 加 -ly 构成，义为「暂时地；暂定地」

senses.title: A condition written into a law or contract
senses.definition: a condition or clause in a law, contract or agreement that states what must be done
senses.definitionCN: 法律、合同或协议中写明必须如何做的条件或条款
senses.example: A provision in the lease forbids keeping pets.
senses.exampleCN: 租约中有一条条款禁止养宠物。
senses.why: Latin provisio meant a seeing ahead, and a clause is exactly foresight written down: the parties decide now what will happen if something goes wrong later.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 provisio 意为「预先看见」，而条款正是被写下来的预见：各方在此刻就定好，以后出了某种情况该怎么办。

senses.title: The act of supplying something
senses.definition: the act of giving or supplying something, especially a service or a resource
senses.definitionCN: 给予或供应某物的行为，尤指服务或资源
senses.example: The provision of clean water is the city's first duty.
senses.exampleCN: 提供干净的饮用水是这座城市的首要职责。
senses.why: Once foresight turns into action, the action is supplying, and English uses the noun for the whole process of making something available.
senses.whyCN: 预见一旦化为行动，这个行动就是供应；英语用这个名词指「使某物可供使用」的整个过程。

senses.title: A store of supplies kept for future use
senses.definition: supplies of food, fuel or equipment kept ready, especially for a journey or an emergency
senses.definitionCN: 备好的食物、燃料或装备，尤指为旅途或应急准备的
senses.example: They laid in provisions before the snow closed the road.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在大雪封路之前备好了给养。
senses.why: What foresight produces is something set aside, so the noun shifts from the act of preparing to the goods sitting in the store room, usually in the plural.
senses.whyCN: 预见所产生的，就是被留出来的东西，于是这个名词从「准备的动作」转到「仓库里堆着的物资」，且常用复数。

senses.title: Preparation made in advance
senses.definition: arrangements made now so that a future need or risk is already taken care of
senses.definitionCN: 现在作出的安排，使将来的需求或风险已被照管到
senses.example: They made provision for their daughter's education years in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 他们多年前就为女儿的教育作了准备。
senses.why: This is the word at its closest to the Latin original: pure forethought, before anything has been handed over or stored.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最贴近拉丁原义的一层：纯粹的预先打算，还没有交出任何东西，也还没有囤起任何东西。

intro.en: Provision comes from a Latin noun of foresight built on the same verb as provide, and English borrowed the noun through French.
intro.cn: provision 来自一个表示「预见」的拉丁语名词，与 provide 建立在同一个动词上；英语是经法语借入这个名词的。

items.en: Videre meant to see, the plain visual root behind the whole family.
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」，是整族词背后那个朴素的「看」的词根。

items.en: Providere meant to see ahead and to take care in advance, with pro- adding the forward direction.
items.cn: providere 意为往前看、提前照料，前缀 pro- 加上了「向前」的方向。

items.en: The noun provisio named the act of foreseeing and the care that followed from it; its stem provis- is what English kept.
items.cn: 名词 provisio 指预见这一动作以及随之而来的照料，英语保留的正是它的词干 provis-。

items.en: Old French provision carried the noun into the senses of supply and of a stipulated arrangement.
items.cn: 古法语 provision 把这个名词带到「供应」与「约定好的安排」这两层意思上。

items.en: Modern English uses the singular for a clause or the act of supplying, and the plural for goods stored up for a journey.
items.cn: 现代英语用单数指条款或供应的行为，用复数指为旅途囤起来的物资。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin verb of seeing ahead; the near-meaning group gathers words for clauses and for what is kept in store.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「预先看见」动词上的词；近义组收表示条款与囤积之物的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to supply or to stipulate.
entries.definitionCN: 表示提供或规定的动词。

entries.definition: Arranged for the present only, to be changed later.
entries.definitionCN: 只为眼前安排的，以后会更改的。

entries.definition: Foresight and care, often seen as guidance from above.
entries.definitionCN: 远见与照料，常被视为来自上方的指引。

entries.definition: Careful about the future, especially with money.
entries.definitionCN: 为将来打算的，尤指用钱谨慎的。

entries.definition: A single condition in a legal document.
entries.definitionCN: 法律文件中的单项条件。

entries.definition: An amount of something available for use.
entries.definitionCN: 可供使用的某物数量。

entries.definition: Goods kept in store for future use.
entries.definitionCN: 为将来使用而存着的货物。

entries.definition: A condition that must be met in an agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 协议中必须满足的条件。

normalIntro.en: The word is foresight that has cooled into an object, and its memories sit on the Latin stem, on the written clause and on the plural in the store room.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是冷却成实物的预见，记忆点落在拉丁词干、写下的条款，以及仓库里的复数形式上。

normal.en: Provision and provide share the Latin verb providere, but the noun came through French while the verb came by another route, which is why the vowel changed.
normal.cn: provision 与 provide 共享拉丁语动词 providere，但名词经法语传来，动词走的是另一条路，所以元音变了。

normal.en: Provis- is the stem of Latin provisio, so the -sion ending was not added in English.
normal.cn: provis- 是拉丁语 provisio 的词干，所以 -sion 并不是英语后来加上的后缀。

normal.en: Provisional keeps the idea of something arranged in advance and adds the hint that the arrangement is only for now.
normal.cn: provisional 保留「事先安排」的意思，并加上「这个安排只管眼前」的意味。

normal.en: In contracts the word means a clause, because a clause is a piece of written foresight.
normal.cn: 在合同里这个词指条款，因为条款就是一段写下来的预见。

normal.en: The plural provisions almost always means food and equipment for a journey, not several clauses.
normal.cn: 复数 provisions 几乎总指旅途所需的食物和装备，而不是好几条条款。

abstract.en: Provision is foresight that has cooled into an object: a clause on paper or a sack in the store room.
abstract.cn: provision 是冷却成实物的预见：要么是纸上的一条条款，要么是仓库里的一袋粮食。

abstract.en: Every contract is a small machine for the future, and its provisions are the parts.
abstract.cn: 每份合同都是一台为未来造的小机器，条款就是它的零件。

abstract.en: To make provision is to admit that the future will ask for something you do not yet need.
abstract.cn: 作出准备，就是承认未来会来索要你此刻还不需要的东西。

examples.en: A provision in the lease forbids keeping pets.
examples.cn: 租约中有一条条款禁止养宠物。

examples.en: The provision of clean water is the city's first duty.
examples.cn: 提供干净的饮用水是这座城市的首要职责。

examples.en: They laid in provisions before the snow closed the road.
examples.cn: 他们在大雪封路之前备好了给养。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若维仁」——听着像「铺若为仁」，先替别人把东西铺好，正是供应与储备。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（在前）+ videre（看见）构成 providere，其名词 provisio（预见、照料）经古法语 provision 进入英语；与 province 不同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is foresight turning into arrangement; the senses divide into the written clause, the act of supplying, the goods stored up, and preparation made in advance.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「预见变成安排」；义项分成写下的条款、供应的行为、囤起来的物资，以及提前作出的准备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sacks stacked against a store room wall, with a sheet of paper beside the door setting out how they will be shared.
core.cn: 核心意象：仓库里一袋袋粮食靠墙码好，门边贴着一张写明分配办法的纸。

branches.en: a clause printed in small type
branches.cn: 用小字印出的一条条款

branches.en: a pipe carrying water into a district
branches.cn: 把水送进街区的一根管道

branches.en: sacks stacked against a store room wall
branches.cn: 靠着仓库墙码起的口袋

branches.en: money set aside years before it is needed
branches.cn: 多年前就留出来的一笔钱

branches.en: a treaty and the grain promised under it
branches.cn: 一份条约以及条约里承诺的粮食

intro.en: A Latin verb of seeing ahead and the noun built from it hold the word together, and French passed the noun on with its stem intact.
intro.cn: 表示「预先看见」的拉丁语动词及由其构成的名词共同支撑这个词，法语连词干一起把它传了下来。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre, to see, providere, to see ahead, and the noun provisio, a foreseeing, are the direct sources of the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre（看见）、providere（往前看）与名词 provisio（预见）是英语这个名词的直接来源。
