definition_zh: 挑衅；激怒；激怒的原因；煽动
definition_en: the act of deliberately making someone angry, or something that stirs a person into reacting
core_image: 有人探身向前，把一根手指点到别人眼前，等着对方跳起来
scene: 酒馆里，一个陌生人故意把椅子撞到旁边那桌，又笑着退回自己的位置，等着看对方怎么反应。He hit back only after repeated provocation and was later judged less harshly.
sceneCN: 这里取「挑衅、激怒」的意思（第 1 个义项：故意惹人发怒的行为）；句意为他在屡次受到挑衅之后才还手，后来因此被从轻看待。陌生人撞椅子的那个动作就是线索。

pos.zh: 挑衅；激怒；激怒的原因；煽动

derivatives.zh: 与 provocation 同出拉丁语 provocare（把人唤出来），义为「激怒；引起」
由拉丁词干 provocat- 加 -ive 构成，义为「挑衅的；煽动性的」
由 provocative 加 -ly 构成，义为「挑衅地」
借自法语，指受雇挑起事端的人，如 agent provocateur

senses.title: The act of deliberately making someone angry
senses.definition: the act of saying or doing something on purpose to make someone angry or to make them react
senses.definitionCN: 故意说或做某事，使某人生气或作出反应的行为
senses.example: He lashed out at the reporter without any provocation.
senses.exampleCN: 他在没有受到任何挑衅的情况下对那名记者发作。
senses.why: Latin provocare meant to call someone forth, like a challenge shouted across a space, so the noun starts as an invitation to fight rather than as an emotion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 provocare 意为「把人叫出来」，像隔着一段距离发出的挑战，所以这个名词的起点是「邀人来战」，而不是某种情绪。

senses.title: Something that causes anger or a reaction
senses.definition: an event or remark that stirs someone into anger or into action
senses.definitionCN: 激起某人愤怒或促使其行动的某个事件或言语
senses.example: The insult was the provocation that started the whole quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 那句侮辱就是引起整场争吵的导火索。
senses.why: If the word names the calling forth, it easily slides to the thing that does the calling: what was an act becomes a cause standing in front of the reaction.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词指「把人叫出来」这件事，就很容易滑到「发出呼唤的那个东西」：原本是一个动作，变成了立在反应之前的起因。

senses.title: Behaviour that reduces blame in law
senses.definition: in law, words or actions that make an ordinary person lose self-control and are therefore weighed when judging the response
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指使常人失去自制的言语或行为，判断回应是否过当时会予以考虑
senses.example: The defence argued that the killing followed severe provocation.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方主张，那起杀人是在受到严重激惹之后发生的。
senses.why: Courts need a name for the pressure that pushes a person past the limit, and this noun supplies it, which is why the word can lighten a sentence while naming no act of the accused.
senses.whyCN: 法庭需要为那种把人逼过界限的压力起个名字，这个名词正好提供；所以它能减轻刑罚，却并不指被告自己的任何动作。

intro.en: Provocation comes from a Latin verb that meant to call someone forth, built from pro-, forward, and vocare, to call; it is unrelated to provide and province.
intro.cn: provocation 来自一个意为「把人叫出来」的拉丁语动词，由 pro-（向前）与 vocare（呼喊）构成；它与 provide、province 都不同源。

items.en: Vocare meant to call, and it is the calling root behind a large Latin family.
items.cn: vocare 意为呼喊，是拉丁语中一大族词背后那个「叫」的词根。

items.en: With pro-, forward, provocare meant to call someone out, to challenge or to stir them to action.
items.cn: 加上表示向前的 pro-，provocare 意为把人叫出来、挑战他或促使他行动。

items.en: The noun provocatio named a calling forth, and in Roman law also a formal appeal against a decision.
items.cn: 名词 provocatio 指「唤出」，在罗马法中也指对裁决的正式上诉。

items.en: Old French borrowed the noun as provocation and narrowed it towards the stirring of anger.
items.cn: 古法语借入该名词作 provocation，并把它收窄到「激起怒气」这一方向。

items.en: Modern English keeps the noun for the act, for the thing that triggers it, and for the legal pressure that explains a reaction.
items.cn: 现代英语保留这个名词，用来指行为本身、触发它的东西，以及法律上能解释某种反应的压力。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin verb of calling out; the near-meaning group gathers words for acts and remarks that sting.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「喊出来」动词上的词；近义组收表示刺伤人的举动与言语的词。

entries.definition: To make someone angry or to stir something up.
entries.definitionCN: 使人发怒，或激起某事。

entries.definition: Likely to annoy people or to stir thought and desire.
entries.definitionCN: 容易惹人恼火，或能激起思考与欲望的。

entries.definition: Someone paid to stir trouble, as in agent provocateur.
entries.definitionCN: 受雇挑起事端的人，如 agent provocateur。

entries.definition: To speak publicly in favour of something.
entries.definitionCN: 公开支持某事。

entries.definition: A remark or act meant to hurt someone's pride.
entries.definitionCN: 意在伤害他人自尊的言语或举动。

entries.definition: A remark made to mock and provoke someone.
entries.definitionCN: 用来嘲笑并激怒他人的话。

entries.definition: The act of urging someone to act, especially wrongly.
entries.definitionCN: 鼓动他人行动，尤指不当行为。

entries.definition: The feeling of being annoyed, or something that causes it.
entries.definitionCN: 恼怒的感觉，或引起恼怒的事物。

normalIntro.en: The word is a call thrown out to someone, and its memories sit on the calling root, on the legal appeal behind it, and on the relatives it gathered along the way.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是朝别人抛出去的一声叫喊，记忆点落在「呼喊」词根、它背后的法律上诉，以及一路收进来的同族词上。

normal.en: Pro- means forward and vocare means to call, so to provoke is literally to call someone out to the front.
normal.cn: pro- 意为向前，vocare 意为呼喊，所以 provoke 字面上就是把人叫到前面来。

normal.en: Provocatio in Roman law was an appeal, so the family has always carried a public, challenging tone.
normal.cn: 罗马法中的 provocatio 是一种上诉，所以这一族词一直带着公开挑战的语气。

normal.en: Provocateur is a French borrowing for a person who stirs trouble on purpose, as in agent provocateur.
normal.cn: provocateur 是来自法语的借词，指故意挑起事端的人，如 agent provocateur。

normal.en: Advocate and provoke share the calling root: one calls someone to your side, the other calls them out.
normal.cn: advocate 与 provoke 共享「呼喊」词根：一个把人叫到你这边，一个把人叫出来对阵。

normal.en: The word is unrelated to provide and province, which come from Latin videre and provincia; only the first syllable looks alike.
normal.cn: 这个词与 provide、province 无关，后两者分别来自拉丁语的 videre 与 provincia；只是开头一个音节看起来相似。

abstract.en: A provocation is a hook thrown out to see what will bite; the word describes the gesture, not the fish.
abstract.cn: 挑衅是抛出的一个钩子，看谁会咬；这个词描述的是动作，不是鱼。

abstract.en: Two people can describe the same act in two directions, one calling it provocation and the other calling it a joke.
abstract.cn: 同一件事，两个人可以从两个方向去称呼：一个叫挑衅，一个叫玩笑。

abstract.en: Law treats provocation as a pressure any ordinary person would feel, which turns a private exchange into a measure of us all.
abstract.cn: 法律把挑衅看成任何常人都承受不住的压力，这就把两个人的争执变成了衡量所有人的尺子。

examples.en: He lashed out at the reporter without any provocation.
examples.cn: 他在没有受到任何挑衅的情况下对那名记者发作。

examples.en: The insult was the provocation that started the whole quarrel.
examples.cn: 那句侮辱就是引起整场争吵的导火索。

examples.en: The defence argued that the killing followed severe provocation.
examples.cn: 辩方主张，那起杀人是在受到严重激惹之后发生的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若佛开申」——听着像「不是佛也开战」，被人一激，凡人也开战，正是挑衅。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ vocare（呼喊）构成 provocare，本义「把人唤出来、挑战」；其名词 provocatio 经古法语 provocation 进入英语。与 provide、provision、province 均不同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a call that dares someone to react; the senses divide into the act of stirring anger, the thing that triggers it, and the pressure the law weighs.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一声挑人回应的叫喊」；义项分成激起怒气的行为、触发它的东西，以及法律会权衡的那股压力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone leaning forward and calling another person out, daring them to step over the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人探身向前，高声把另一个人叫出来，挑他越过那条线。

branches.en: a stranger knocking a chair into another table
branches.cn: 陌生人把椅子撞到别人桌上

branches.en: a shouted dare across a crowded room
branches.cn: 拥挤屋子里隔空喊出的挑战

branches.en: a single insult that ends a quiet dinner
branches.cn: 一句侮辱结束了安静的晚餐

branches.en: a barrister describing words that pushed a man past his limit
branches.cn: 律师描述那些把人逼过界限的话

branches.en: the same remark taken as insult here and as excuse there
branches.cn: 同一句话在此处是侮辱、在彼处是理由

intro.en: A Latin prefix of forward movement and a Latin verb of calling hold the word together, and the same stem then grows an adjective, an adverb and a French borrowing.
intro.cn: 表示向前的拉丁语前缀与表示呼喊的拉丁语动词共同支撑这个词，同一词干随后长出形容词、副词和一个法语借词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vocare, to call, the compound provocare, to call forth or challenge, and the noun provocatio are the direct sources of the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vocare（呼喊）、复合形式 provocare（唤出、挑战）与名词 provocatio 是英语这个名词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 激怒；挑衅；引发；引起；煽动
definition_en: to stir someone into anger or action, or to cause a reaction or an event
core_image: 有人把一根长杆伸进静止的水面，圈圈波纹从杆尖向外荡开
scene: 这份提案把两边的旧账都翻了出来，会上争了两个小时。The proposal provoked a long debate in the council.
sceneCN: 这里指引起一场争论（第 3 个义项：引发反应或讨论）；句意为这份提案在议会引发了长时间辩论。图中可辨识物件：伸进水面的长杆、向外荡开的波纹、静止的水；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 激怒；挑衅；引发；引起

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「挑衅；激怒；诱因」
由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「挑衅的；煽动的；引人深思的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「挑衅地」
由该动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「气人的；惹人恼的」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「挑衅者」（少用）

senses.title: To make someone angry
senses.definition: to stir a person into anger, often deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 使某人动怒，常带故意成分
senses.example: His remarks provoked the crowd outside the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 他的话激怒了厅外的人群。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to call forth, and anger is one of the things called out of a person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「唤出」，而怒气正是从人身上被唤出来的东西之一。

senses.title: To challenge deliberately
senses.definition: to invite a fight or a strong reaction by confronting someone on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意顶撞某人，以招来争斗或强烈反应
senses.example: The guard was provoked into opening the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 门卫被激得打开了大门。
senses.why: Provocation is a call the other person is expected to answer, which is why it feels like an invitation.
senses.whyCN: 挑衅是一声预期对方会回应的召唤，所以才像一份邀请。

senses.title: To give rise to a reaction
senses.definition: to cause a response, discussion or public reaction without any intent to anger
senses.definitionCN: 引起回应、讨论或公众反应，不含激怒意图
senses.example: The report provoked wide discussion in the press.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告在报界引发广泛讨论。
senses.why: The oldest neutral sense simply calls a response into being, with no emotional charge.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的中性义只是把回应唤出来，不带情绪色彩。

senses.title: To arouse interest
senses.definition: to make curiosity or interest appear in someone
senses.definitionCN: 使某人产生好奇或兴趣
senses.example: The strange photograph provoked her curiosity.
senses.exampleCN: 那张奇怪的照片引起了她的好奇。
senses.why: Curiosity is another response that is called forth rather than pushed in.
senses.whyCN: 好奇也是被唤出的回应，而不是被塞进去的。

senses.title: To stir an emotion
senses.definition: to bring a strong feeling such as fear, pity or laughter to the surface
senses.definitionCN: 使恐惧、怜悯或笑意等强烈情绪浮到表面
senses.example: The empty street provoked a sense of unease.
senses.exampleCN: 空荡的街道激起一种不安。
senses.why: Emotions are treated as things that can be summoned, which is the core of the Latin verb.
senses.whyCN: 情绪被当作可以召唤的东西，这正是拉丁动词的核心。

senses.title: To draw criticism
senses.definition: to cause disapproval, complaint or public objection
senses.definitionCN: 引起不满、投诉或公开反对
senses.example: The decision provoked protests from residents.
senses.exampleCN: 这一决定招致居民的抗议。
senses.why: Criticism is a response with a negative charge, but the mechanism is still calling forth.
senses.whyCN: 批评是一种带负电的回应，但机制仍是「唤出」。

senses.title: To trigger an attack or symptom
senses.definition: to set off a physical episode such as a cough, a fit or an allergic response
senses.definitionCN: 触发咳嗽、发作或过敏反应等身体事件
senses.example: Cold air provoked a coughing fit.
senses.exampleCN: 冷空气诱发了一阵咳嗽。
senses.why: Medicine uses the verb for anything that sets a latent condition going.
senses.whyCN: 医学用这个动词指任何让潜伏状况启动的因素。

senses.title: To incite action
senses.definition: to urge a group towards collective action, often unrest
senses.definitionCN: 鼓动一群人采取集体行动，常指骚动
senses.example: leaflets provoked a march the next morning.
senses.exampleCN: 传单煽动了第二天早上的游行。
senses.why: A crowd is called into motion, and the verb keeps the image of a call rather than a push.
senses.whyCN: 人群被唤起来行动，这个动词保留「召唤」而非「推动」的画面。

intro.en: Provoke comes from Latin provocare, to call forth or challenge, from pro-, forth, and vocare, to call, from vox, voice. English took it through French in the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 provocare「唤出、挑战」，由 pro-「向前」与 vocare「呼叫」构成，而 vocare 出自 vox「声音」；英语十四世纪经法语引入。

items.en: Vox meant voice, and it is the source of vocal, voice and the whole calling family.
items.cn: 这个词意为「声音」，是 vocal、voice 以及整个「呼叫」词族的来源。

items.en: Vocare meant to call or summon, and it built verbs such as invoke, evoke and revoke.
items.cn: 这个词意为呼叫、召唤，构成了 invoke、evoke、revoke 等动词。

items.en: The prefix meant forward or forth, so provocare pictured a call sent out towards someone.
items.cn: 前缀意为向前、向外，所以这个词的画面是把呼唤朝某人发出去。

items.en: The verb meant to call forth, to challenge, and in law to appeal against a decision.
items.cn: 这个动词意为唤出、挑战，在法律中指对裁决提出上诉。

items.en: English adopted the verb through French; the exact first date is uncertain and is usually given only as that century.
items.cn: 英语经法语采用这个动词；确切首见年代不确定，通常只给「十四世纪」。

items.en: The sense of stirring anger became dominant later, while the neutral sense of causing a response survives in formal writing.
items.cn: 「激起怒气」后来越来越占主导，而「引起回应」的中性义在正式写作中仍存活。

note.en: The first group shares the call root or looks close; the second group names neighbouring ideas of causing and stirring.
note.cn: 第一组与「provoke」共享「呼叫」词根或只是形近；第二组是与「引起、激起」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of stirring someone or something up.
entries.definitionCN: 指激怒、挑起这一行为的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective for something that stirs a reaction or desire.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指挑衅的、引人反应的。

entries.definition: To call out a memory or feeling, with the prefix meaning out.
entries.definitionCN: 指唤出记忆或情感，前缀意为「向外」。

entries.definition: To call upon, as a law or a power, with the prefix meaning in.
entries.definitionCN: 指援引法律或力量，前缀意为「向内」。

entries.definition: To call back, hence to cancel a right or a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 指唤回，因而指撤销权利或规定。

entries.definition: The stock of words, from the same voice root.
entries.definitionCN: 指词汇总量，同出「声音」词根。

entries.definition: To annoy mildly, with less drama than provoke.
entries.definitionCN: 指轻度惹恼，戏剧性不如本词。

entries.definition: To set off an event or reaction, often mechanically.
entries.definitionCN: 指触发事件或反应，常带机械意味。

entries.definition: To wake a feeling or interest in someone.
entries.definitionCN: 指唤起情感或兴趣。

entries.definition: To urge people towards violent or unlawful action.
entries.definitionCN: 指煽动人们采取暴力或违法行动。

entries.definition: To draw out a response or information, usually without anger.
entries.definitionCN: 指引出回应或信息，通常不含怒气。

entries.definition: To bother someone mildly and repeatedly.
entries.definitionCN: 指反复轻度打扰某人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the voice root, its four sibling verbs, and the neutral and angry branches of meaning.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「声音」词根、它的四个兄弟动词，以及中性义与激怒义两条分支。

normal.en: Vox is voice, so provoke is to send a call out and wait for an answer.
normal.cn: vox 是「声音」，所以这个词是发出一声召唤，等着回应。

normal.en: Invoke, evoke and revoke share the same calling root with different prefixes.
normal.cn: invoke、evoke、revoke 与它共享同一「呼叫」词根，只是前缀不同。

normal.en: Provoke a debate is neutral; provoke a crowd is not.
normal.cn: 「引发辩论」是中性说法，「激怒人群」则不是。

normal.en: Provocation and provocative are the noun and adjective of the same action.
normal.cn: 它的名词与形容词形式分别表示「挑衅」与「挑衅的」。

normal.en: Cold air can provoke a cough, which shows how wide the neutral sense reaches.
normal.cn: 冷空气能诱发咳嗽，可见中性义覆盖面之广。

abstract.en: To provoke is to open a door and refuse to say what is behind it.
abstract.cn: 激怒，就是打开一扇门却不说门后有什么。

abstract.en: Every provocation is a question the other person is expected to answer badly.
abstract.cn: 每一次挑衅，都是一个预期对方会答坏的问题。

abstract.en: A response called forth is not the same as a response forced in, and that difference is the word.
abstract.cn: 被唤出的回应与被塞进去的回应不同，这个差别就是这个词本身。

examples.en: The cartoon provoked angry letters from both sides.
examples.cn: 这幅漫画招致双方愤怒的来信。

examples.en: Her question provoked a thoughtful silence.
examples.cn: 她的问题引来一阵沉思的沉默。

examples.en: Dust can provoke an asthma attack in sensitive people.
examples.cn: 粉尘可能诱发敏感人群的哮喘发作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普罗沃克」——长杆一伸，水面荡开圈圈波纹：引发、激怒

root: 拉丁语 vox「声音」→ vocare「呼叫」→ provocare「唤出、挑战」（pro-「向前」+ vocare）；英语十四世纪经法语引入。与 evoke、invoke、revoke 同根不同前缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all call something forth: anger, a challenge, a reaction, curiosity, emotion, criticism, a symptom and collective action.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在把某物唤出：怒气、挑战、反应、好奇、情绪、批评、症状与集体行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pole touches still water and rings spread outward from the point of contact.
core.cn: 核心意象：长杆触到静水，圈圈波纹从触点向外荡开。

branches.en: THE INVITATION TO ANGER: someone is deliberately stirred and expected to react.
branches.cn: 向怒气发出邀请：某人被有意激起，并被期待作出反应。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC ANSWER: a report or a decision draws discussion, criticism or protest.
branches.cn: 公众的回应：报告或决定引出讨论、批评或抗议。

branches.en: THE SPARK OF CURIOSITY: interest appears because something strange is placed in view.
branches.cn: 好奇的火星：奇怪之物被摆在眼前，兴趣随之出现。

branches.en: THE SURFACING FEELING: fear, pity or laughter is brought up from below.
branches.cn: 浮上来的情绪：恐惧、怜悯或笑意从底下被带上来。

branches.en: THE LATENT EPISODE: a symptom starts, or a crowd is moved into action.
branches.cn: 潜伏的发作：症状启动，或人群被鼓动起来。

intro.en: Provoke is a Latin verb of calling, and the prefix is the piece that decides which way the call goes.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示「呼叫」的拉丁动词，前缀决定这声呼唤朝哪个方向去。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies vox, vocare and provocare; the pieces are well recorded, so no part of the word is marked uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 vox、vocare、provocare；这些部件有清楚记录，这个词没有哪一部分标为存疑。

items.example: The noun is the source of the whole calling family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个「呼叫」词族的源头。

items.example: It built invoke, evoke and revoke.
It sends the call out towards someone.
items.exampleCN: 它把呼唤朝某人发出去。

items.example: The verb carried both the neutral and the combative shades.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词兼有中性义与好斗色彩。

senses.title: Belonging to the mind
senses.definition: relating to the mind and its processes of thought, feeling and perception
senses.definitionCN: 与心智及其思维、情感与知觉过程相关
senses.example: Sleep loss has both physical and psychological consequences.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠不足既有生理后果，也有心理后果。
senses.why: Psyche meant 'breath, soul, mind'. Psychological marks whatever belongs to that inner life rather than to the body's machinery.
senses.whyCN: psychē 意为“气息、灵魂、心智”。psychological 标记属于这种内在生活、而非身体机制的东西。

senses.title: Of the discipline
senses.definition: belonging to psychology as an academic or clinical field
senses.definitionCN: 属于作为学术或临床领域的心理学
senses.example: The paper appeared in a leading psychological journal.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文发表在一份顶尖心理学期刊上。
senses.why: Once psychology became a laboratory science in the 19th century, psychological came to mean 'of the discipline', covering experiments, journals and clinics.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪心理学成为实验室科学之后，psychological 开始指“属于该学科的”，涵盖实验、期刊与诊所。

senses.title: Working through feeling
senses.definition: affecting a person through emotions and mental state rather than physical force
senses.definitionCN: 通过情绪与心理状态而非物理力量影响人
senses.example: The threat of redundancy caused psychological harm long before any job was lost.
senses.exampleCN: 裁员的威胁在任何岗位真正消失之前就已造成心理伤害。
senses.why: The word names effects that travel through the mind: fear, shame or anxiety can do damage even when no physical injury occurs.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名经由心智传导的影响：恐惧、羞耻或焦虑即使没有身体伤害，也能造成损伤。

senses.title: Based on mental measurement
senses.definition: measured or assessed through mental tests and reported feelings rather than physical instruments
senses.definitionCN: 通过心理测试与自述感受而非物理仪器来测量或评估
senses.example: The trial used psychological scales to rate anxiety before and after treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 试验用心理量表评定治疗前后的焦虑程度。
senses.why: Research needed a word for data that comes from questionnaires and scales, so psychological marks the measuring method as well as the subject.
senses.whyCN: 研究需要为来自问卷与量表的数据找个词，于是 psychological 既标记研究对象，也标记测量方法。

senses.title: An edge in the mind
senses.definition: giving an advantage by affecting confidence, fear or motivation rather than resources
senses.definitionCN: 通过影响信心、恐惧或动机而非资源来取得优势
senses.example: Winning the first set gave the team a psychological advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 赢下第一盘给这支队伍带来了心理优势。
senses.why: Competition uses the adjective for edges that exist only in the mind: the score is level, but one side already feels beaten or emboldened.
senses.whyCN: 竞争用这个形容词指只存在于心里的优势：比分持平，但一方已感到被击败或受到鼓舞。

senses.title: Written from the inside
senses.definition: of a novel or film: focused on inner motives and feelings rather than external action
senses.definitionCN: 指小说或电影聚焦内心动机与感受，而非外部动作
senses.example: Critics praised the novel as a psychological study of grief.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称赞这部小说是对悲伤的心理研究。
senses.why: Literary criticism borrowed the term for works that stay inside a character's mind, where plot matters less than motive.
senses.whyCN: 文学批评借这个词指留在人物内心的作品，在这类作品中情节不如动机重要。

senses.title: The right moment for the mind
senses.definition: of a moment: judged to be the point when people are most ready to accept something
senses.definitionCN: 指被人判断为最易接受某事的时刻
senses.example: He waited for the psychological moment to raise the question of funding.
senses.exampleCN: 他等待心理上最合适的时机提出经费问题。
senses.why: The fixed phrase 'the psychological moment' treats timing as a mental condition: the instant when resistance is lowest and attention highest.
senses.whyCN: 固定说法“心理上的时机”把时机当作一种心理状态：阻力最低、注意最高的那一刻。

senses.title: Fought through the mind
senses.definition: of warfare or tactics: aimed at beliefs, morale and fear instead of physical targets
senses.definitionCN: 指针对信念、士气与恐惧而非物理目标的战争或战术
senses.example: Leaflets and broadcasts were part of a psychological campaign against the garrison.
senses.exampleCN: 传单与广播构成了针对守军的心理战的一部分。
senses.why: Military language uses the adjective when the target is morale: nothing is destroyed, yet the will to fight is attacked directly.
senses.whyCN: 军事语言在目标是士气时用这个形容词：没有东西被摧毁，但战斗意志被直接攻击。

intro.en: Psychological joins Greek psychē, 'breath, soul, mind', with logos, 'word, account, reason', through the Latin-formed psychologia. The -ical ending comes from Latin -icalis and Greek -ikos. The word began as a label for the study of the soul and ended up covering stress, novels, morale and warfare.
intro.cn: psychological 把希腊语 psychē“气息、灵魂、心智”与 logos“言说、道理、理性”结合，经由拉丁形式的 psychologia 而来。-ical 词尾来自拉丁 -icalis 与希腊 -ikos。这个词最初是“研究灵魂”的标签，后来覆盖压力、小说、士气与战争。

items.en: Psyche meant 'breath, life, soul'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; it is generally connected with the idea of breathing, though no root is proved.
items.cn: psychē 意为“气息、生命、灵魂”。其更深来源不确定，一般认为与“呼吸”的观念有关，但没有被证实的词根。

items.en: Logos meant 'word, account, reason'. Combined with other stems, -logia named a field of study or a body of discourse.
items.cn: logos 意为“言说、记述、理性”。与其他词干结合时，-logia 命名一个研究领域或一套论述。

items.en: The compound psychologia was coined in Latin by 16th-century scholars for the study of the soul, before any laboratory existed.
items.cn: 复合词 psychologia 由 16 世纪学者在拉丁语中造出，指对灵魂的研究，当时还没有任何实验室。

items.en: English formed psychological from psychology with the adjective suffix -ical, at first meaning 'of the soul or mind'.
items.cn: 英语用形容词后缀 -ical 从 psychology 造出 psychological，最初意为“属于灵魂或心智的”。

items.en: Wundt and others turned psychology into an experimental discipline, and psychological came to cover measurement, tests and clinical practice.
items.cn: 冯特等人把心理学变成实验学科，psychological 随之覆盖测量、测验与临床实践。

items.en: Psychological warfare was named in the two world wars, psychological novels flourished earlier in the century, and the adjective spread to stress, advantage and timing.
items.cn: 心理战在两次世界大战中得名，心理小说在 20 世纪初兴盛，这个形容词又扩散到压力、优势与时机。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the adjective from psychology, the adverb and the different-root physiological. The meaning group contrasts mental, emotional and cognitive descriptions.
note.cn: 形近组区分形容词与 psychology、副词，以及词根不同的 physiological；词义组比较 mental、emotional 与 cognitive 三类描述。

entries.definition: the study of the mind, or a person's mental make-up. It names the field, while psychological describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 对心智的研究，或某人的心理构成。它命名字科，而 psychological 描述属于该学科的东西。

entries.definition: in mental terms. It turns the adjective into a statement about how something affects the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 在心理层面上。它把形容词转为关于如何影响心智的陈述。

entries.definition: relating to the body's functions. It looks parallel but comes from physis 'nature' plus logos, a different stem from psyche.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体功能相关的。它看起来结构平行，却来自 physis“自然”加 logos，词干与 psychē 不同。

entries.definition: relating to the medical treatment of mental illness. It comes from iatreia 'healing', not from logos 'study'.
entries.definitionCN: 与精神疾病的医学治疗相关的。它来自 iatreia“治疗”，而非 logos“研究”。

entries.definition: relating to the mind. It is the plain everyday word and often pairs with health and illness, while psychological is more technical.
entries.definitionCN: 与心智相关的。它是平实的日常词，常与健康、疾病搭配，而 psychological 更技术化。

entries.definition: relating to feelings. It covers one part of mental life, while psychological covers the whole inner system.
entries.definitionCN: 与情感相关的。它覆盖心理生活的一部分，而 psychological 覆盖整个内在系统。

entries.definition: relating to thinking, memory and perception. It names the intellectual side rather than feeling or morale.
entries.definitionCN: 与思维、记忆和知觉相关的。它指理智的一面，而非情绪或士气。

entries.definition: existing in a person's own experience. It marks the private side of what psychological studies measure.
entries.definitionCN: 存在于个人自身经验中的。它标记心理研究所测之物的私人一面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into psyche and logos, then let the inner-life picture cover stress, science, novels, advantage, timing and warfare.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词拆成 psyche 与 logos，再用内在生活的画面覆盖压力、科学、小说、优势、时机与战争。

normal.en: Split it as psyche + log + ical: mind + study + adjective. Psychological means 'of the study of the mind'.
normal.cn: 拆成 psyche + log + ical：心智、研究、形容词。psychological 意为“关于心智研究的”。

normal.en: Picture a head opened like a room, with feelings drifting around instead of gears.
normal.cn: 想象一个像房间一样打开的头，里面飘着情绪而不是齿轮。

normal.en: Physical harm hits the body; psychological harm hits the same person through fear and shame.
normal.cn: 物理伤害打身体；心理伤害通过恐惧与羞耻打同一个人。

normal.en: A psychological novel stays inside that room, watching motives instead of events.
normal.cn: 心理小说留在那个房间里，看动机而不是看事件。

normal.en: Psychological warfare attacks morale, so the target is that room rather than any building.
normal.cn: 心理战攻击士气，因此目标就是那个房间，而不是任何建筑。

abstract.en: Keep the two Greek halves visible: psyche is the subject, logos is the way of studying it.
abstract.cn: 让两个希腊部分保持可见：psychē 是对象，logos 是研究方式。

abstract.en: Notice that the adjective can describe both a science and a trick: the same word covers journals and warfare.
abstract.cn: 注意这个形容词既能描述科学也能描述手段：同一个词覆盖期刊与战争。

abstract.en: Contrast it with physiological: one studies the mind, the other the body, even though the words look like twins.
abstract.cn: 与 physiological 对照：一个研究心智，一个研究身体，尽管两词看起来像双胞胎。

examples.en: Researchers measured the psychological effects of isolation on long voyages.
examples.cn: 研究者测量了长期航行中隔离对心理的影响。

examples.en: The coach said the early goal gave his players a psychological lift.
examples.cn: 教练说那个早早的进球让球员们在心理上受到鼓舞。

examples.en: The museum mounted a psychological warfare exhibition from the cold war.
examples.cn: 博物馆举办了一场冷战心理战展览。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“赛可乐鸡扣”：赛场上喝口可乐，鸡血一扣，心理状态立刻不同。

root: 希腊 psychē“气息、灵魂、心智”加 logos“言说、研究”构成 psychologia，加 -ical 为形容词；核心是“属于心智及其研究”。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses point to the inner life: a mind that suffers, a science that studies it, an effect that travels through feeling, a scale that measures it, an advantage that lives in confidence, a novel that stays inside it, a moment when it is ready, and a war that attacks it directly.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指向内在生活：会受苦的心智、研究它的科学、经由情绪传导的影响、测量它的量表、存在于信心中的优势、留在它内部的小说、它准备好的时刻，以及直接攻击它的战争。

core.en: The inner life of a person, and everything that acts on it or measures it.
core.cn: 一个人的内在生活，以及作用于它或测量它的一切。

branches.en: SUBJECT: the mind itself and the discipline that studies it.
branches.cn: 对象：心智本身以及研究它的学科。

branches.en: EFFECT: harm or advantage arrives through feeling, not force.
branches.cn: 影响：伤害或优势经由情绪而非力量到来。

branches.en: MEASURE: scales and tests turn inner states into data.
branches.cn: 测量：量表与测验把内在状态变成数据。

branches.en: FICTION: a narrative stays inside motive rather than action.
branches.cn: 虚构：叙事留在动机内部，而非外部动作。

branches.en: TIMING AND WAR: the mind is either ready to yield or actively attacked.
branches.cn: 时机与战争：心智要么准备好让步，要么正被主动攻击。

intro.en: Psychological is psyche plus logos plus the adjective suffix -ical. The items below follow the Greek stems into nouns, adverbs and neighbouring disciplines.
intro.cn: psychological 由 psyche、logos 与形容词后缀 -ical 构成。下列条目沿着这两个希腊词干走到名词、副词与邻近学科。

latinIntro.en: The Greek entries give the two stems. They explain why psychology, psychiatry and psychosomatic all begin with the same word for soul.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语条目给出两个词干，解释了为什么 psychology、psychiatry 与 psychosomatic 都以同一个表示“灵魂”的词开头。

items.meaning: relating to the mind or its study
items.exampleCN: 这项调查追踪心理康复情况。

items.meaning: a person who studies the mind
items.example: A psychologist assessed the child's anxiety.
items.exampleCN: 一位心理学家评估了孩子的焦虑。
工人们在心理上已精疲力竭。

items.meaning: relating to the mind; also claiming extra-sensory powers
items.example: He claimed psychic experiences during the experiment.
items.exampleCN: 他声称在实验中有通灵体验。

items.meaning: the medical treatment of mental illness
items.example: Psychiatry treated the trauma with therapy and drugs.
items.exampleCN: 精神病学用治疗与药物处理创伤。

items.meaning: of symptoms caused or worsened by mental factors
items.meaningCN: 心身的；由心理因素引起的
items.exampleCN: 这皮疹被判断为心身性的。

items.meaning: the soul or mind as a whole
items.example: The myth describes the trials of Psyche.
items.exampleCN: 这个神话描述了普绪克的试炼。

latinEntries.meaning: the breath of life; the mind
a field of study or discourse

definition_en: a building or room where alcoholic drinks are served and drunk, especially in Britain; also, in Australia and New Zealand, a hotel with a bar
core_image: 傍晚街角亮起暖灯的小店，木门一推开就是碰杯声
scene: 下班铃响过，几个人把工具袋往肩上一搭，拐进街角那家挂着旧木牌的小店。After the shift, the crew walked down to the pub on the corner for a quick drink.
sceneCN: 这里 pub 是「酒馆」（第 1 个义项：英国供人坐下喝酒的场所）；句意为下工之后，工人们走到街角那家酒馆喝一杯。图中可辨识物件：旧木牌、暖灯、吧台。

pos.zh: 酒馆；酒吧；（澳新）旅店

derivatives.zh: 与 public 同源、经营酒馆的人；英式英语指酒馆老板，拉丁语原义是包税人
pub 与 crawl 复合，指一晚连喝好几家酒馆
pub 加表示「常去者」的 -goer，指常泡酒馆的人

senses.title: A place where alcoholic drinks are served
senses.definition: a building or room, especially in Britain, where people sit and buy alcoholic drinks to drink there
senses.definitionCN: 尤指英国的建筑或房间，人们坐在里面买酒并当场饮用
senses.example: We met in a quiet pub behind the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站后面一家安静的酒馆碰了头。
senses.why: Pub is public house cut short, and a public house was simply a house open to the public for drink, so the short form still names a room anyone may walk into.
senses.whyCN: pub 是 public house（向公众开放的房子）的截短，而 public house 本就是指「对公众开放、可以进去喝酒的房子」，所以短词仍指谁都能推门进去的那间屋子。

senses.title: A hotel with a bar in Australia and New Zealand
senses.definition: in Australia and New Zealand, a hotel that has a bar and often also serves meals and lets rooms
senses.definitionCN: 在澳大利亚与新西兰，指带酒吧的旅店，常兼供饭食并出租房间
senses.example: They stayed two nights at the pub beside the highway.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在公路边那家旅店住了两晚。
senses.why: On the long colonial roads one building sold drink, cooked meals and let a bed, so the word for the drinking room widened to cover the whole hotel.
senses.whyCN: 在漫长的殖民时期公路边，一栋房子同时卖酒、做饭、租床位，于是原本指饮酒房间的词扩大到了整间旅店。

senses.title: The local pub as a neighbourhood meeting place
senses.definition: the nearby pub understood as a regular social centre where neighbours meet and exchange news
senses.definitionCN: 把附近那家酒馆看作固定聚点，邻居在那里见面、交换消息
senses.example: The village pub is where everyone hears the news first.
senses.exampleCN: 村里那家酒馆是所有人最先听到消息的地方。
senses.why: The same room serves the same street every evening, so a business turns into the place where a neighbourhood talks, and English lets the old word carry that role too.
senses.whyCN: 同一间屋子每晚招待同一条街的人，一门生意便变成了街坊说话的地方，英语让这个旧词一并承担这重角色。

senses.title: Of or happening in a pub, used before a noun
senses.definition: used before another noun to mean served, held, or happening in a pub
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一个名词前，表示「酒馆供应的、酒馆里举办的」
senses.example: Sunday pub lunches are a habit in this town.
senses.exampleCN: 周日去酒馆吃午饭是这个镇上的习惯。
senses.why: Once pub names a place, it can stand in front of another noun and mark that thing as belonging to the place, which is exactly how pub food and pub quizzes are formed.
senses.whyCN: pub 一旦指某个场所，就能站到另一个名词前面，标明那样东西属于这个场所，pub food 与 pub quiz 正是这样构成的。

intro.en: Pub is not inherited from Latin but clipped from the English phrase public house in the nineteenth century; the public part of that phrase goes back to Latin publicus, from populus, the people.
intro.cn: pub 并非直接从拉丁语继承而来，而是十九世纪从英语短语 public house 截短而成；其中 public 可上溯到拉丁语 publicus，而 publicus 又来自 populus（人民）。

items.en: Populus meant the people taken as one body, and it is the root behind the adjective publicus.
items.cn: populus 意为作为整体的人民，是形容词 publicus 背后的词根。

items.en: Publicus meant belonging to the people or the state, that is, open to all citizens rather than held privately.
items.cn: publicus 意为「属于人民或国家的」，也就是向全体公民开放、而非私人占有。

items.en: From the later seventeenth century English called an inn or tavern a public house, a house open to the public for eating and drinking.
items.cn: 十七世纪后期起，英语把客栈、酒馆称作 public house，即向公众开放、供人饮食的房子。

items.en: In the nineteenth century, first in British working speech, the phrase was cut down to the single syllable pub, and the short form spread quickly.
items.cn: 十九世纪，先是英国劳工阶层口语把这个短语截成单音节 pub，短形式很快传开。

items.en: Modern English uses pub for the British drinking place, for the Australian hotel, and inside compounds such as pub quiz, pub food and pub-crawl.
items.cn: 现代英语用 pub 指英国的饮酒场所、澳新的旅店，也用在 pub quiz、pub food、pub-crawl 这类复合词里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the phrase pub was cut from and its Latin relatives; the near-meaning group gathers other words for places that sell drink.
note.cn: 形近组收 pub 被截短之前的短语与它的拉丁同族词；近义组收其他表示卖酒场所的词。

entries.definition: The full form that pub was cut from: a house open to the public for food and drink.
entries.definitionCN: pub 被截短之前的完整形式：向公众开放、供饮食的房子。

entries.definition: In British English the keeper of a pub; the Latin word once meant a tax farmer.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语中指酒馆老板；这个拉丁词原本指包税人。

entries.definition: Open to all people, or the people as a whole; the adjective inside public house.
entries.definitionCN: 向所有人开放的，或指全体民众；public house 里用的正是这个形容词。

entries.definition: To make a text available to the public; built on the same Latin family as public.
entries.definitionCN: 使文字向公众发行；与 public 同出一个拉丁词族。

entries.definition: A counter or room where drinks are served and drunk.
entries.definitionCN: 供应并供人饮用酒水的柜台或房间。

entries.definition: An old word for a place that sells drink and often food.
entries.definitionCN: 指卖酒、常兼供食物的旧词。

entries.definition: A small hotel that also serves meals and drink.
entries.definitionCN: 兼供饭食与酒水的小旅店。

entries.definition: A bar, especially in the old American West.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指美国旧西部的酒吧。

normalIntro.en: The word is a three-word phrase squeezed into one syllable, and behind that phrase stands a Latin adjective for what belongs to the people.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把一个三词短语压成了一个音节，而短语背后是一个表示「属于人民」的拉丁形容词。

normal.en: Pub is public house cut short: the endings fall away and two words become one syllable.
normal.cn: pub 是 public house 的截短：词尾脱落，两个词压缩成一个音节。

normal.en: The public in public house is Latin publicus, from populus, the people, so a pub was a house open to the people.
normal.cn: public house 里的 public 来自拉丁 publicus，而 publicus 出自 populus（人民），所以 pub 原本就是对人民开放的房子。

normal.en: A publican runs the pub, although the same Latin word once meant a tax collector, a very different trade.
normal.cn: publican 是经营酒馆的人，尽管同一个拉丁词从前指收税的人，两者行当大不相同。

normal.en: Pub quiz and pub lunch keep pub in front of a noun, marking something that happens inside that place.
normal.cn: pub quiz 与 pub lunch 把 pub 放在名词前，标明那件事就发生在这个场所里。

normal.en: In Australia and New Zealand one word covers the bar and the bedrooms, because one building once did both jobs.
normal.cn: 在澳大利亚与新西兰，一个词同时覆盖酒吧与客房，因为从前一栋房子就兼做这两件事。

abstract.en: The word is a door swinging open on a warm evening, with strangers sitting close enough to talk.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是一扇在暖夜里推开的门，里面的陌生人坐得近到可以交谈。

abstract.en: Cutting a long phrase down to one beat is how a language makes room for the thing people do most often.
abstract.cn: 把一个长短语砍成一个节拍，是语言在为人们最常做的事腾出位置。

abstract.en: A pub sells drink, but people come back for the same three chairs and the same familiar noise.
abstract.cn: 酒馆卖的是酒，可人们回来找的是同样那三把椅子和同样熟悉的喧闹。

examples.en: We had lunch at a pub by the river.
examples.cn: 我们在河边一家酒馆吃了午饭。

examples.en: The pub closes at eleven on weekdays.
examples.cn: 这家酒馆工作日十一点关门。

examples.en: He now runs the pub his grandfather opened.
examples.cn: 他现在经营着祖父当年开的那家酒馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「帕布」——推门进去，帕布一声放下杯子，就是街角那家酒馆。

root: pub 是英语短语 public house（向公众开放的房子）在十九世纪的截短形式；public 出自拉丁语 publicus，publicus 又来自 populus（人民）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a house open to the public for drink; the senses divide into the British drinking room, the Australian hotel, the role of neighbourhood centre, and the attributive use before another noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「向公众开放、可供饮酒的房子」；义项由此分出英式饮酒场所、澳新旅店、街坊聚点的角色，以及放在名词前的定语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corner doorway with a warm lamp above it, swinging open on a room full of talk.
core.cn: 核心意象：街角一扇挂着暖灯的门，被推开，里面满是说话声。

branches.en: a warm doorway on a wet evening
branches.cn: 雨夜里透出暖光的一扇门

branches.en: the same three chairs filled every night
branches.cn: 每晚都坐满的同样三把椅子

branches.en: a highway inn with rooms above the bar
branches.cn: 公路旁楼上带客房的旅店

branches.en: a chalkboard listing Sunday lunches
branches.cn: 写着周日午餐的小黑板

branches.en: one word for a room and for a habit
branches.cn: 一个词既指一间屋子，也指一种习惯

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin noun for the people, the adjective built on it, the English phrase public house, and the clipped form pub.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示人民的拉丁名词、由它构成的形容词、英语短语 public house，以及截短形式 pub 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

a quiz held in a pub

definition_zh: 公共的；公开的；公众的；公众；公开场合
definition_en: open for everyone to use or see, not hidden, and relating to the people as a whole; also the people themselves
core_image: 广场中央的一盏灯，四面都照得到，谁走近都能看清
scene: 广场的公告栏刚换上新的通知，路过的行人都停下来读那几行字。The council made the plan public only after every resident had been told.
sceneCN: 这里 public 是「公开的、不再保密的」（第 2 个义项）；句意为在通知到每位居民之后，市政会才把方案公开。图中可辨识物件：公告栏、通知纸、驻足的路人。

pos.zh: 公共的；公开的；公众的
公众；民众；公开场合

derivatives.zh: public 加名词后缀 -ity，义为「宣传；曝光度」
public 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「公开地」
同出拉丁 publicare（使公开），义为「出版；发表」
来自拉丁 res publica（公共之事），义为「共和国」
public 加动词后缀 -ize，义为「宣传；使公开」

senses.title: Available for everyone to use
senses.definition: provided for all people to use, rather than for one person or a small group
senses.definitionCN: 供所有人使用，而不是供某个人或某个小圈子使用
senses.example: The public library stays open until nine.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公共图书馆开到晚上九点。
senses.why: The Latin adjective named what belonged to the people as a body, so a thing held in common rather than privately was called public.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词本指「属于人民全体的」，因此凡由众人共有、不由私人占有的东西，就被称作 public。

senses.title: Known or seen by everyone
senses.definition: known or seen by everyone, with nothing kept secret
senses.definitionCN: 所有人都知道或看见的，没有任何部分被保密
senses.example: The report became public after the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 审判结束后，这份报告被公开了。
senses.why: If something belongs to all the people, hiding it from them makes no sense, so shared ownership slides into shared knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西既然属于全体人民，瞒着他们就没有道理，于是「共有」自然滑向「共知」。

senses.title: Relating to the people or the state
senses.definition: relating to the people as a whole, or to work done by the state on their behalf
senses.definitionCN: 与全体人民有关，或与以人民名义运作的国家事务有关
senses.example: Public spending on roads fell last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年用于道路的公共开支下降了。
senses.why: Money and decisions that concern everyone are handled in the name of all, so the adjective also marks what the state holds rather than what a private owner holds.
senses.whyCN: 涉及所有人的钱和决定都以全体之名来打理，所以这个词也用来标明由国家、而非私人掌握的事物。

senses.title: The people as a whole
senses.definition: the people of a country or community considered as one body, especially as readers, viewers or voters
senses.definitionCN: 把一个国家或社区的人看作一个整体，尤指读者、观众或选民
senses.example: The gallery opened its doors to the public at ten.
senses.exampleCN: 美术馆十点向公众开门。
senses.why: The adjective was used so often with a noun left unsaid that it became a noun itself, naming the crowd a place is open to.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词常与一个被省略的名词连用，久而久之自己变成了名词，专指场所向其开放的那群人。

senses.title: An open setting where others can see and hear
senses.definition: an open place or setting where other people can see and hear what happens
senses.definitionCN: 一个开放的场景，别人能看见、听见发生的事
senses.example: She has never sung in public before.
senses.exampleCN: 她以前从未在公开场合唱过歌。
senses.why: A public place is one open to all, so the noun in the phrase in public names that open setting itself, in contrast with a private room.
senses.whyCN: public 的地方就是对所有人开放的地方，因此 in public 中的名词正指这个开放场景本身，与私密房间相对。

intro.en: Public came into English through French from Latin publicus, an adjective built on populus, the people; the noun use is a later English development.
intro.cn: public 经法语从拉丁语 publicus 进入英语，publicus 是由 populus（人民）构成的形容词；名词用法是英语后来发展出来的。

items.en: Populus meant the people as a body, and it is the base from which publicus was formed.
items.cn: populus 意为作为整体的人民，是构成 publicus 的基础。

items.en: Publicus meant belonging to the people or the state; an older form poplicus is recorded, which shows the link with populus.
items.cn: publicus 意为「属于人民或国家的」；文献中还有更早的形式 poplicus，可见它与 populus 的联系。

items.en: Old French took the adjective as public with the same sense of open and common, and passed it into English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词写作 public，保留「开放的、共有的」意思，十五世纪传入英语。

items.en: English began using public as a noun for the people, first in phrases such as in public and then standing alone with the definite article.
items.cn: 英语开始把 public 用作指人民的名词，先出现在 in public 这类短语中，后来能单独与定冠词连用。

items.en: Modern English builds public transport, public health and public opinion, and pairs public with private as opposite poles.
items.cn: 现代英语构成 public transport、public health、public opinion 等说法，并把 public 与 private 配成对立的两极。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers English words built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what is shared or open.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一拉丁词干上的英语词；近义组收表示「共有、开放」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for attention from the media, formed with -ity.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -ity 构成、指媒体关注的名词。

entries.definition: To make a text available to the public, from Latin publicare.
entries.definitionCN: 使文字向公众发行，出自拉丁语 publicare。

entries.definition: A state whose head is elected, from Latin res publica, the public thing.
entries.definitionCN: 元首经选举产生的国家，出自拉丁语 res publica（公共之事）。

entries.definition: A British pub keeper; the Latin word meant a tax farmer.
entries.definitionCN: 英国的酒馆老板；这个拉丁词原指包税人。

entries.definition: Shared by a group rather than owned by one person.
entries.definitionCN: 由群体共用，而非一人独占的。

entries.definition: Done or held by all the members of a group together.
entries.definitionCN: 由群体全体成员共同做出或持有的。

entries.definition: Not closed or hidden, and free for anyone to enter.
entries.definitionCN: 未关闭、未隐藏，任何人都可进入的。

entries.definition: Relating to a town and the duties of the people who live there.
entries.definitionCN: 与城镇及居民义务有关的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin adjective for what belongs to the people, and English later let it stand alone as a noun for those people.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是表示「属于人民」的拉丁形容词，英语后来让它单独作名词，指那些人民。

normal.en: Public came through French from Latin publicus, an adjective built on populus, the people.
normal.cn: public 经法语来自拉丁 publicus，而 publicus 是由 populus（人民）构成的形容词。

normal.en: The noun public is the adjective standing alone, naming the people a place is open to.
normal.cn: 名词 public 就是单独站立的形容词，指场所向其开放的那群人。

normal.en: Public and private form a pair: one belongs to all, the other belongs to one person or one household.
normal.cn: public 与 private 成对：前者属于所有人，后者属于一个人或一个家庭。

normal.en: Publicity is public with -ity and publicly is public with -ly, and both keep the same idea of openness.
normal.cn: publicity 是 public 加 -ity，publicly 是 public 加 -ly，两者都保留着同一层「开放」的意思。

normal.en: Publish comes from Latin publicare, to make public, which is why publishing is always an act aimed at readers.
normal.cn: publish 出自拉丁 publicare（使公开），所以出版始终是朝着读者做出的动作。

abstract.en: The word is a lamp in the middle of a square: no side of the square is darker than another.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是广场中央的一盏灯：广场的任何一边都不会比另一边更暗。

abstract.en: A matter turns public when the cost of hiding it grows higher than the cost of showing it.
abstract.cn: 一件事之所以转为公开，往往是因为隐瞒的代价高过了示人的代价。

abstract.en: English keeps one word for shared ownership, shared knowledge and shared space, as if all three were one openness.
abstract.cn: 英语用同一个词涵盖共有、共知与共用空间，仿佛这三者本就是同一种开放。

examples.en: The park is public land, so anyone may walk there.
examples.cn: 这座公园是公共土地，任何人都可以进去散步。

examples.en: Details of the deal were made public yesterday.
examples.cn: 交易的细节昨天被公开了。

examples.en: He rarely speaks in public.
examples.cn: 他很少在公开场合讲话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「帕布立克」——广场上人人都立着看得见，记住 public 是公共的、公开的。

root: 拉丁语 populus（人民）→ publicus（属于人民的）→ 古法语 public → 英语 public；加 -ity 得 publicity，加 -ly 得 publicly，词义核心都是「向所有人开放」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what belongs to all the people; the senses divide into shared use, shared knowledge, state affairs, the people themselves, and the open setting.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「属于全体人民的东西」；义项由此分为共同使用、共同知晓、国家事务、人民本身，以及开放的场景。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp at the centre of a square, lighting every side of it evenly.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场正中的一盏灯，把四面照得一样亮。

branches.en: a library door with no ticket desk
branches.cn: 没有售票台的图书馆大门

branches.en: a lamp that leaves no corner dark
branches.cn: 一盏不留下暗角的灯

branches.en: a road paid for out of common funds
branches.cn: 用公共资金修起来的路

branches.en: a crowd waiting for the gallery to open
branches.cn: 等着美术馆开门的人群

branches.en: a first song sung before strangers
branches.cn: 第一次在陌生人面前唱歌

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin noun for the people, the adjective built on it, and the English endings -ity and -ly that turn it into a noun and an adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示人民的拉丁名词、由它构成的形容词，以及把它变成名词与副词的英语后缀 -ity、-ly 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 公开性；公众所知的状态

definition_zh: 出版；出版物；发表；公布；发行
definition_en: the act of making something known to everyone, and the printed or digital thing that results when writing is issued to the public
core_image: 一叠写好的稿子被推到印刷机下，几分钟后变成成千上万份，散到所有陌生人手里
scene: 研究员不断刷新期刊页面，等待着那期正式出刊。The publication of the March issue was delayed until June.
sceneCN: 这里 publication 是「发表」（第 3 个义项：使研究或文章为公众可得）；句意：发表不等于录用——论文三月被录用，但那期六月才出。画面里有屏幕、校样和日历；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Putting a book into the world
senses.titleCN: 出版：把一本书推进世界
senses.definition: the act of producing a book, magazine, or other work and offering it to the public
senses.definitionCN: 制作书籍、杂志或其他作品并向公众提供的行为
senses.example: The publication of her memoir took two years.
senses.exampleCN: 她回忆录的出版花了两年时间。
senses.why: The sense 'issuing of a written or printed work to the public by sale or distribution' is recorded from the 1570s. The older 'making known' turns into a physical process: print, bind, sell.
senses.whyCN: “通过销售或分发向公众发行文字或印刷作品”这一义项记录于 16 世纪 70 年代。更早的“使人知晓”变成了物理过程：印刷、装订、销售。

senses.title: The thing issued: a publication
senses.titleCN: 出版物：被推出去的那件东西
senses.definition: a book, journal, or other work that has been published
senses.definitionCN: 已出版的书籍、期刊或其他作品
senses.example: The library subscribes to several scientific publications.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆订阅了几种科学出版物。
senses.why: From the 1650s the word also names the thing issued and offered. The noun of action becomes a countable object — the deed and its product share one form.
senses.whyCN: 从 17 世纪 50 年代起，这个词也命名被发行、被提供的那个东西。动作名词变成了可数物体——行为与产物共用同一个形式。

senses.title: Making research public
senses.titleCN: 发表：把研究交到同行手里
senses.definition: the act of making research, writing, or an article available to the public, especially in a journal
senses.definitionCN: 使研究、文字或文章为公众可得的行为，尤指在期刊上
senses.example: Publication in a peer-reviewed journal is required for promotion.
senses.exampleCN: 在同行评审期刊上发表是晋升的必要条件。
senses.why: Academic life narrowed the 1570s issuing sense to the author's act: a paper is 'published' when it enters the public record. Publication becomes the currency of a career.
senses.whyCN: 学术生活把 16 世纪 70 年代的发行义收窄为作者的行为：论文进入公共记录即“发表”。publication 于是成了学术生涯的通货。

senses.title: Making it known: the original sense
senses.titleCN: 公布、公开宣布：最初的那个意思
senses.definition: the act of making something publicly known; official notification to the people at large
senses.definitionCN: 使某事为公众所知的行为；向大众的官方通告
senses.example: The publication of the findings surprised the whole industry.
senses.exampleCN: 研究结果的公布震动了整个行业。
senses.why: Late 14c. publicacioun meant 'the act of making publicly known, notification to the people at large'. Before print, publication was simply speech made public.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪后期的 publicacioun 意为“使公众知晓的行为、向大众通告”。在印刷术之前，publication 只是把话公开说出来。

senses.title: The release of an edition
senses.titleCN: 发行、发售：某一版次被放出去
senses.definition: the release of a particular edition or issue for sale or distribution
senses.definitionCN: 某一版本或期次为销售或分发而发行
senses.example: The publication of the new edition was timed for the holidays.
senses.exampleCN: 新版的发行被安排在假期。
senses.why: Once publication is an event in the market, it can be scheduled, delayed, and dated. The abstract act becomes a release date on a calendar.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 publication 成为市场中的事件，它就可以被排期、推迟、标注日期。抽象的行为变成了日历上的发行日。

senses.title: A periodical you can hold
senses.titleCN: 刊物：按期出的一本东西
senses.definition: a periodical, such as a magazine or journal, issued at regular intervals
senses.definitionCN: 定期发行的期刊，如杂志或学报
senses.example: She writes a column for a trade publication.
senses.exampleCN: 她为一家行业刊物撰写专栏。
senses.why: The object sense specializes: a publication is not any book but one of a series that keeps appearing. The issue is the unit, the publication is the title.
senses.whyCN: 物体义发生专门化：publication 不是任意一本书，而是持续出现的一系列中的一种。一期是单位，publication 是刊名。

senses.title: Exposing private material
senses.titleCN: 披露、公开：把私下的东西摊到阳光下
senses.definition: the act of making private letters, records, or images open to public view
senses.definitionCN: 使私人信件、记录或影像向公众开放的行为
senses.example: The publication of the private letters caused a scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 这些私人信件的公开引发了一场丑闻。
senses.why: The original 'making known' sense survives strongly when the material was never meant to be known. Publication here is exposure, not commerce.
senses.whyCN: 当材料本不该被知道时，最初的“使人知晓”义就强烈地存活着。这里的 publication 是曝光，而不是买卖。

senses.title: Publication in media law
senses.titleCN: 法律上的传播、发表：让第三方看到
senses.definition: in media law, the communication of defamatory or protected material to a third party
senses.definitionCN: 媒体法中，向第三方传播诽谤性或受保护材料的行为
senses.example: The court asked whether the email amounted to publication.
senses.exampleCN: 法院要判断这封电子邮件是否构成“传播”。
senses.why: Law needs a precise moment when words leave private hands. 'Publication' supplies it: any communication to a third party, even one reader, can be publication.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一个精确的时刻，判定言语何时离开私人之手。publication 提供了它：向第三方——哪怕只有一位读者——的任何传达都可构成“传播”。

senses.title: The publishing trade
senses.titleCN: 出版业、出版工作：这一行的总称
senses.definition: the business or activity of publishing as a profession
senses.definitionCN: 作为职业的出版业务或活动
senses.example: She has worked in publication for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在出版行业工作了二十年。
senses.why: The noun of action can name an entire trade, just as 'education' names a field. What began as one act of making public becomes an industry.
senses.whyCN: 动作名词可以命名整个行业，正如 education 命名一个领域。最初“使公开”的一个动作，变成了一个产业。

intro.en: Publication is from Latin publicare 'make public', built on publicus 'of the people'. It begins as the act of telling everyone, gains the printing sense in the 1570s, and then splits into the act, the object, the edition, and the law.
intro.cn: publication 来自拉丁语 publicare“使公开”，其基础是 publicus“属于人民的”。它起初指“告诉所有人”的行为，16 世纪 70 年代获得印刷义，随后分裂为行为、物体、版次与法律义。

items.en: Publicare meant 'to make public', from publicus 'of the people, common'. Publicus was altered from Old Latin poplicus, from populus 'people'; the deeper origin of populus is uncertain and is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: publicare 意为“使公开”，来自 publicus“属于人民的、公共的”。publicus 由古拉丁语 poplicus 变来，后者来自 populus“人民”；populus 更深的来源不确定，标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Publicatio meant 'a making public', also 'an adjudging to the public treasury'. The legal sense of handing something to the state runs beside the sense of announcing.
items.cn: publicatio 意为“使公开”，也指“判归国库”。把某物交给国家的法律义，与“宣布”的义项并行。

items.en: Publicacioun enters English as 'the act of making publicly known, notification to the people at large'. Print does not exist yet; publication is an act of speech and notice.
items.cn: publicacioun 进入英语时意为“使公众知晓的行为、向大众通告”。印刷术尚未出现；publication 是一种言说与公告的行为。

items.en: The meaning 'the issuing of a written or printed work to the public by sale or distribution' is recorded by the 1570s. The printing press gives the word a product.
items.cn: “通过销售或分发向公众发行文字或印刷作品”这一义项记录于 16 世纪 70 年代。印刷机给了这个词一个产品。

items.en: From the 1650s the word also names the thing so issued and offered. Act and object now share one noun.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪 50 年代起，这个词也命名被发行、被提供的那个东西。行为与物体如今共用一个名词。

items.en: Academic publication becomes a career measure, periodicals multiply, and media law fixes 'communication to a third party' as publication. The old 'making known' sense survives in every one.
items.cn: 学术发表成为职业衡量标准，期刊大量增加，媒体法把“向第三方传达”确定为 publication。古老的“使人知晓”义在每一个新义里都存活下来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the publ- opening or the -ation ending but differs in meaning; the near group names the act, the object, and the audience.
note.cn: 形近组共享 publ- 开头或 -ation 结尾，但意义不同；近义组则分别命名行为、物体与受众。

entries.definition: attention given to someone by the media. It ends in -ity and names attention, not an issued work.
entries.definitionCN: 媒体给予的公众关注。它以 -ity 结尾，指注意力，而不是被发行的作品。

entries.definition: the act of publicizing something. It looks like publication but its ending is -ization, not -ation.
entries.definitionCN: 宣传、使公开的行为。它形似 publication，但词尾是 -ization 而非 -ation。

entries.definition: the act of publishing something again. The prefix re- marks a second issuing.
entries.definitionCN: 再出版；重新发表。前缀 re- 标记第二次发行。

entries.definition: a tavern keeper or, in older use, a tax collector. It shares the publi- opening but ends in -an, not -ation.
entries.definitionCN: 酒馆老板，旧时也指收税人。它共享 publi- 开头，但词尾是 -an 而非 -ation。

entries.definition: the business of producing books and periodicals. It names the trade, where publication can name a single act or object.
entries.definitionCN: 图书与期刊的生产行业。它命名行业，而 publication 可指单次行为或单个物体。

entries.definition: a particular edition or number of a periodical, or the act of releasing it.
entries.definitionCN: 期刊的某一版次或期号，或发行它的行为。

entries.definition: the act of making a film, record, or statement available to the public.
entries.definitionCN: 使电影、唱片或声明向公众可得的行为。

entries.definition: a public statement that informs people of something. It matches publication's original sense.
entries.definitionCN: 告知公众某事的公开声明。它对应 publication 的本义。

entries.definition: the number of copies of a publication sold or distributed.
entries.definitionCN: 出版物售出或分发的份数。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin publicus 'of the people', publicare 'make public', and the 1570s printing sense that turned an announcement into an object.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 publicus“属于人民的”、publicare“使公开”，以及 16 世纪 70 年代把公告变成物品的印刷义。

normal.en: publication = public + -ation: the act of making something public.
normal.cn: publication = public + -ation：使某物公开的行为。

normal.en: publicare 'make public' is the same verb behind publish: publication is the noun of that act.
normal.cn: publicare“使公开”也是 publish 背后的动词：publication 就是那个动作的名词。

normal.en: Before print, publication was a voice in the square; after print, it is a book on a shelf.
normal.cn: 印刷术之前，publication 是广场上的一个声音；印刷术之后，它是书架上的一本书。

normal.en: A publication can be both the deed and the thing: 'the publication of the book' and 'a scientific publication'.
normal.cn: publication 既可以是行为也可以是东西：“这本书的出版”和“一份科学出版物”。

normal.en: In law, publication needs only a third pair of eyes — even one reader can count.
normal.cn: 在法律上，publication 只需要第三双眼睛——哪怕只有一位读者也算。

abstract.en: The core is a door opened: what was private becomes available to all.
abstract.cn: 核心是一扇被打开的门：原本私下的东西变成人人可得。

abstract.en: One act, three products: knowledge, a printed object, and an industry.
abstract.cn: 一个动作，三种产物：知识、一件印刷品、一个产业。

abstract.en: The word keeps its original promise: publication is first of all making known.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终守着最初的承诺：publication 首先是使人知晓。

examples.en: The publication of the report was delayed by legal review.
examples.cn: 报告的公布因法律审查而推迟。

examples.en: She lists three publications on her academic CV.
examples.cn: 她在学术简历上列了三项出版物。

examples.en: The newspaper is a daily publication with a large circulation.
examples.cn: 这份报纸是一份发行量很大的日报。

dict_mnemonic.text: public（公众）+ ation（行为）——把东西送到公众面前；谐音“帕布利凯申”：把稿子“扑”到印刷机上，公开（public）地发出去 → publication 出版；公布

root: 源自拉丁语 publicare“使公开”，由 publicus“属于人民的”加动词后缀构成，名词 publicatio 经古法语进入英语；核心是“把原本私下的东西交给所有人”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses on one movement: from private to public. The word begins as an announcement, becomes the printing and sale of a work, then the work itself, an edition, a periodical, an exposure, a legal communication, and finally an industry.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围绕同一个动作：从私下到公开。这个词从“公告”开始，变成作品的印刷与销售，再指作品本身、一个版次、一种期刊、一次曝光、一次法律意义上的传达，最后指一个行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a private manuscript pushed through the press and handed out to strangers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份私人手稿被送进印刷机，然后分发到陌生人手里。

branches.en: THE ACT OF ISSUING: producing a work, and releasing a particular edition.
branches.cn: 发行行为：制作一部作品，以及发行某个版次。

branches.en: THE THING ISSUED: a published work, and a periodical that keeps appearing.
branches.cn: 被发行之物：已出版的作品，以及持续出现的期刊。

branches.en: MAKING KNOWN: academic publication, and the original sense of public announcement.
branches.cn: 使人知晓：学术发表，以及公开宣告的本义。

branches.en: EXPOSURE: private material brought into the light, willing or not.
branches.cn: 曝光：私人材料被带到光下，无论当事人是否愿意。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC SPHERE: publication in media law, and publishing as a trade.
branches.cn: 公共领域：媒体法中的“传播”，以及作为行业的出版。

intro.en: Publication is publ- plus -ication. Its family shows Latin publicus 'of the people', the verb publicare, the noun ending -ation, and the agent and quality endings -er, -ist, -ity and -ize.
intro.cn: publication 是 publ- 加 -ication。它的词族展示拉丁语 publicus“属于人民的”、动词 publicare、名词词尾 -ation，以及施事与性质词尾 -er、-ist、-ity、-ize。

latinIntro.en: Latin publicus 'of the people' is the base of public, publish and publication; publicare 'make public' yields publication and publication's verb publish, while -ity and -ize build publicity and publicize.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 publicus“属于人民的”是 public、publish、publication 的基础；publicare“使公开”给出 publication 及其动词 publish，而 -ity 与 -ize 构成 publicity 与 publicize。

items.meaning: the act of making public; a published work
items.example: The publication of the atlas took ten years.
items.exampleCN: 这本图集的出版花了十年。

items.meaning: open to all; the people as a whole
items.example: The garden is open to the public.

items.meaning: to make public; to issue a work
items.example: They publish four issues a year.

items.meaning: a person or company that issues works
items.exampleCN: 出版商接受了她的手稿。

items.meaning: to bring something to public attention
items.example: The team publicized the event on social media.
items.exampleCN: 团队在社交媒体上宣传了这场活动。

items.meaning: the state of being known; media attention
items.exampleCN: 这场审判带来了不受欢迎的关注。
她的公关安排了三场采访。

items.example: The republication includes a new preface.
The draft is not yet publishable.

items.meaning: the stage before a work is published
items.exampleCN: 出版前的样书被送到了评论者手中。

definition_zh: 宣传；曝光度；公众关注；宣传材料
definition_en: the attention that a person or thing gets from the media and the public; the work of attracting such attention; material issued to promote something
core_image: 聚光灯打到舞台中央，台下无数镜头同时抬起来
scene: 新店开张前一周，街口的广告牌、手机推送和报纸角落都在说同一件事。The little bakery got more publicity from one photograph than from a year of advertising.
sceneCN: 这里 publicity 是「媒体关注、曝光度」（第 1 个义项：来自媒体与公众的注意）；句意为这家小面包店靠一张照片得到的关注，胜过一整年的广告。图中可辨识物件：广告牌、聚光灯、镜头。

pos.zh: 宣传；曝光度；公众关注；宣传材料

derivatives.zh: public 加动词后缀 -ize，义为「宣传；推广」
public 加表人后缀 -ist，义为「公关人员；宣传员」
去掉名词后缀 -ity 得到的形容词，义为「公共的；公开的」

senses.title: Attention from the media and the public
senses.definition: the attention that a person, product or event receives from newspapers, television and the public
senses.definitionCN: 人、产品、事件从报纸、电视和公众那里获得的注意
senses.example: The court case brought the family unwanted publicity.
senses.exampleCN: 这场官司给这家人带来了他们并不想要的关注。
senses.why: Publicity is the noun form of public, so it names the state of being seen by everyone; the media only make that state visible.
senses.whyCN: publicity 是 public 的名词形式，本指「被所有人看见的状态」，媒体只是把这种状态变得看得见。

senses.title: The work of attracting public attention
senses.definition: the business or activity of persuading the public to notice a product, a person or an event
senses.definitionCN: 设法让公众注意某个产品、人物或事件的工作
senses.example: She works in publicity for a film company.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家电影公司做宣传工作。
senses.why: Once being seen has value, somebody must produce that visibility, so the noun also names the deliberate work of drawing eyes.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「被看见」有了价值，就得有人去制造这种可见度，于是这个词也指刻意把目光引过来的工作。

senses.title: Material issued to promote something
senses.definition: printed or filmed material sent out to tell the public about something
senses.definitionCN: 为向公众介绍某事而发出的印刷品或影像材料
senses.example: The hotel sent publicity to every travel agent in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店给城里每一家旅行社都寄了宣传材料。
senses.why: The work of publicity produces sheets, pictures and short films, and the same noun can stand for the things it hands out.
senses.whyCN: 宣传工作会产出文稿、图片和短片，同一个名词也就能指它发出去的那些东西。

senses.title: The condition of being open to public knowledge
senses.titleCN: 公开性；为人所知的状态
senses.definition: the state of a matter being open to public knowledge rather than kept private
senses.definitionCN: 一件事向公众知识开放、而非被私下保留的状态
senses.example: The publicity of the hearing was itself part of the punishment.
senses.exampleCN: 这场听证的公开本身就是惩罚的一部分。
senses.why: Behind the media sense sits an older legal idea that a matter belongs to the public, and the noun can still name that openness on its own.
senses.whyCN: 媒体义项背后是更早的法律观念：一件事属于公众，这个名词至今仍能单指这种公开状态。

intro.en: Publicity is public plus the noun ending -ity, modelled on a medieval Latin noun and on French publicité; its first English sense was the state of being public, and the media sense came later.
intro.cn: publicity 是 public 加名词后缀 -ity，以中世纪拉丁名词与法语 publicité 为范本；英语最早的义项是「公开的状态」，媒体义项是后来才有的。

items.en: Publicus meant belonging to the people, and from it Latin built nouns for the quality of being public.
items.cn: publicus 意为「属于人民的」，拉丁语由它造出表示「公开性质」的名词。

items.en: Medieval Latin publicitas named the quality of being public, and it is generally thought to have supplied the model for the French and English forms.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 publicitas 指「公开的性质」；一般认为这个名词为法语和英语的形式提供了范本。

items.en: French publicité widened the sense to making something known to the public, and English borrowed the word in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 publicité 把词义扩大到「使公众知晓某事」，英语在十八世纪借入这个词。

items.en: English publicity first meant the state of being public, then shifted to the business of drawing public attention as newspapers and advertising grew.
items.cn: 英语 publicity 先指「公开的状态」，随着报纸与广告的发展，转而指「吸引公众注意的行当」。

items.en: Modern English uses publicity for media attention, for the promotion industry, and for the sheets and clips that industry sends out.
items.cn: 现代英语用 publicity 指媒体关注、宣传行业，以及该行业发出的文稿与片段。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for attention and for the work of getting it.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的形式；近义组收表示「关注」以及「争取关注的工作」的名词。

entries.definition: Open to all, or the people as a whole; the adjective behind publicity.
entries.definitionCN: 向所有人开放的，或指全体民众；publicity 背后的形容词。

entries.definition: To make something widely known on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 有意让某事广为人知。

entries.definition: A person paid to keep a name in the papers.
entries.definitionCN: 受雇让某个名字持续见报的人。

entries.definition: To issue a text for the public to read.
entries.definitionCN: 把文字发行出来供公众阅读。

entries.definition: Activity that helps sell or popularize something.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助销售或推广某事物的活动。

entries.definition: The state of being seen or discussed by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 被许多人看到或谈论的状态。

entries.definition: Paid messages that persuade people to buy.
entries.definitionCN: 付费的、说服人们购买的信息。

entries.definition: Loud claims that inflate interest in something.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事物的热度吹高的说法。

normalIntro.en: The noun is the adjective public with -ity attached, and both go back to the Latin quality of being open to the people.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词是形容词 public 加上 -ity，两者都回到拉丁语「向人民开放」这一性质。

normal.en: Publicity is public with -ity, an ending that turns a quality into a noun, so it names the state of being public.
normal.cn: publicity 是 public 加 -ity，这个后缀把性质变成名词，所以它指「处于公开状态」。

normal.en: The Latin model is publicitas, a medieval noun for exactly that quality.
normal.cn: 它的拉丁范本是 publicitas，一个正指这种性质的中世纪名词。

normal.en: Publicity and publicist share a stem: one is the attention, the other is the person paid to produce it.
normal.cn: publicity 与 publicist 同词干：前者是关注，后者是受雇制造关注的人。

normal.en: Publicize is the verb, and it means to make something public on purpose.
normal.cn: publicize 是对应的动词，意为有意把某事公开。

normal.en: A publicity stunt is a planned act whose only real purpose is to be reported.
normal.cn: publicity stunt 是一种安排好的举动，唯一真正的目的就是被报道。

abstract.en: The word is a spotlight switched on: before it, a thing merely exists; after it, everyone has an opinion.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是一盏打开的聚光灯：亮之前东西只是存在，亮之后人人都有了看法。

abstract.en: Attention can be manufactured, not only received, which is why one noun covers the light and the people who aim it.
abstract.cn: 关注可以被制造，而不只是被接受，所以同一个名词既指那束光，也指操纵光的人。

abstract.en: When privacy is sold, publicity becomes a price, and the same word names the bill.
abstract.cn: 当隐私被拿去交换，曝光就成了一种价格，同一个词也用来指那张账单。

examples.en: The film got plenty of publicity before it opened.
examples.cn: 这部电影上映前就获得了大量宣传。

examples.en: He hired a firm to handle publicity for the tour.
examples.cn: 他请了一家公司为巡演做宣传。

examples.en: The case attracted publicity across the country.
examples.cn: 这起案件在全国范围内引起了关注。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「帕布利瑟提」——把东西摆到人人都看得见的灯下，就是 publicity，宣传与曝光。

root: 拉丁语 publicus（属于人民的）→ 中世纪拉丁 publicitas（公开的性质）→ 法语 publicité → 英语 publicity；由 public 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，核心是「被公众看见」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being open to the public eye; the senses divide into media attention, the work of attracting it, the material sent out, and the bare state of openness.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「暴露在公众目光之下」；义项由此分为媒体关注、争取关注的工作、发出的材料，以及纯粹的公开状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spotlight striking the middle of a stage while every camera below lifts at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：聚光灯打在舞台中央，台下所有镜头同时抬起。

branches.en: one photograph reprinted in a hundred papers
branches.cn: 一张照片被上百家报纸转载

branches.en: a name repeated until strangers recognize it
branches.cn: 一个名字被重复到陌生人也能认出

branches.en: a desk of staff ringing editors all morning
branches.cn: 一整个上午给编辑打电话的办公桌

branches.en: an envelope of glossy sheets for travel agents
branches.cn: 寄给旅行社的一叠光面宣传页

branches.en: a hearing held with the doors left open
branches.cn: 大门敞开举行的听证

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin adjective for what belongs to the people and by the English noun ending -ity, which names a quality or state.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「属于人民」的拉丁形容词和指性质、状态的名词后缀 -ity 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 公开地；当众；公然地；由公众（出资或所有）
definition_en: in a way that many people can see or hear; openly and without hiding anything; by the state or by the public as a whole
core_image: 一个人站到台上，把手里那张纸举过头顶，让全场都看得见
scene: 会场原本嘈杂，主持人走上台，请大家安静下来。She publicly apologized to the staff she had blamed the week before.
sceneCN: 这里 publicly 是「当众、公开地」（第 1 个义项：在别人看得见听得见的地方做某事）；句意为她当众向自己上周错怪的员工道歉。图中可辨识物件：台子、话筒、举起的一页纸。

pos.zh: 公开地；当众；公然地；由公众出资或所有

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「公共的；公开的」
同族名词，义为「宣传；曝光度」
同源动词，义为「出版；发表」
同族动词，义为「宣传；使公开」

senses.title: In front of other people
senses.definition: in a place or way where other people can see and hear what is done
senses.definitionCN: 在别人看得见、听得见的地方或以这样的方式
senses.example: He publicly thanked the nurses who had saved him.
senses.exampleCN: 他当众感谢了救过他的护士们。
senses.why: Publicly is public plus -ly, so it describes an act done in the open, where the public can witness it.
senses.whyCN: publicly 是 public 加 -ly，所以它描述的是在开放场合做出、公众能够目睹的动作。

senses.title: Openly, without hiding anything
senses.definition: in an open way that conceals nothing, even when the truth is uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 以不隐瞒任何东西的开放方式，即使真相令人难堪
senses.example: The company publicly admitted that the safety test had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司公开承认那次安全测试没有通过。
senses.why: What is done before everyone cannot easily be denied afterwards, so the adverb also carries the force of refusing to conceal.
senses.whyCN: 当着所有人的面做的事，事后难以否认，所以这个副词也带着「拒绝隐瞒」的力度。

senses.title: By the state or by the public as a whole
senses.definition: by the government, or with money and ownership that belong to everyone
senses.definitionCN: 由政府，或以属于所有人的资金与所有权
senses.example: The library is publicly funded but privately run.
senses.exampleCN: 这家图书馆由公共资金资助，却由私人运营。
senses.why: Because public also means belonging to the people, the adverb can mark who pays for or owns something rather than who watches it.
senses.whyCN: 因为 public 也指「属于人民的」，这个副词就能标明某事由谁出资、归谁所有，而不只是由谁观看。

senses.title: In a form open to everyone
senses.titleCN: 向公众开放地；可公开获取地
senses.definition: in a form that anyone is allowed to read, use or attend
senses.definitionCN: 以任何人都可以阅读、使用或参加的形式
senses.example: The data are publicly available on the council website.
senses.exampleCN: 这些数据在市政会网站上可以公开获取。
senses.why: The same openness that lets people watch an act also lets them reach a record, so the adverb extends from visible action to accessible information.
senses.whyCN: 允许人看见某个举动的开放性，也同样允许人查到某份记录，于是这个副词从可见的行为延伸到可取用的信息。

intro.en: Publicly is the English adverb made by adding -ly to public, and public goes back through French to Latin publicus, built on populus, the people.
intro.cn: publicly 是英语在 public 后加 -ly 构成的副词，而 public 经法语上溯到拉丁 publicus，publicus 由 populus（人民）构成。

items.en: Populus meant the people as a body, and it underlies the whole family of public words.
items.cn: populus 意为作为整体的人民，是整个 public 词族的基础。

items.en: Publicus meant belonging to the people or the state, hence open to all rather than private.
items.cn: publicus 意为「属于人民或国家的」，因此是向所有人开放、而非私有的。

items.en: Old French kept the adjective as public and handed it to English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语保留形容词形式 public，十五世纪把它交给英语。

items.en: English used public as adjective and, later, as a noun for the people, before any adverb existed.
items.cn: 英语先把 public 用作形容词，后来又用作指人民的名词，那时还没有副词形式。

items.en: The adverb ending -ly was added straight to public, giving publicly; the c is kept and no letter is dropped or doubled.
items.cn: 副词后缀 -ly 直接加在 public 后得到 publicly；词尾的 c 保留，既不脱落字母也不双写。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs for saying or doing something in the open.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的词；近义组收表示「公开说出或做出」的副词。

entries.definition: Open to all, or the people as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 向所有人开放的，或指全体民众。

entries.definition: Attention from the media, or the work of attracting it.
entries.definitionCN: 媒体关注，或争取关注的工作。

entries.definition: To issue a text so that the public may read it.
entries.definitionCN: 把文字发行出来供公众阅读。

entries.definition: To make something known to as many people as possible.
entries.definitionCN: 让尽可能多的人知道某事。

entries.definition: Without hiding anything from other people.
entries.definitionCN: 不向他人隐瞒任何事地。

entries.definition: In a way that is done in plain sight.
entries.definitionCN: 在众目睽睽之下做出地。

entries.definition: As it appears on the outside, whatever the inner state.
entries.definitionCN: 不论内心如何，表面上呈现地。

entries.definition: In an honest and direct way.
entries.definitionCN: 诚实而直接地。

normalIntro.en: The word is simply public with the adverb ending -ly, and it keeps the adjective's sense of being open to everyone.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 public 加副词后缀 -ly，保留了形容词「向所有人开放」的意思。

normal.en: Publicly is public plus -ly, with no letter added or dropped.
normal.cn: publicly 就是 public 加 -ly，既没有多写也没有少写字母。

normal.en: The -ly ending marks manner, so publicly answers the question how: in an open way.
normal.cn: -ly 标示方式，所以 publicly 回答的是「怎样做」：以开放的方式。

normal.en: Publicly owned and publicly funded point to the owner or the payer, not to the audience.
normal.cn: publicly owned 与 publicly funded 指向所有者和出资者，而不是观众。

normal.en: Publicly available stretches the same openness to records and data.
normal.cn: publicly available 把同一种开放性延伸到记录与数据上。

normal.en: The adverb never names the public itself; that job belongs to the noun public.
normal.cn: 这个副词从不指公众本身；那件事由名词 public 承担。

abstract.en: The word is a hand lifting a sheet above the head so that even the back row can read it.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是一只手把纸举过头顶，让最后一排也读得到。

abstract.en: Openness has two faces here: being watched, and being reachable.
abstract.cn: 这里的开放性有两面：被人看见，以及被人够得着。

abstract.en: What is said publicly cannot afterwards be quietly unsaid.
abstract.cn: 公开说出口的话，事后没法悄悄地收回去。

examples.en: She publicly refused the offer at the meeting.
examples.cn: 她在会上当众拒绝了这个提议。

examples.en: The bridge is publicly owned and free to cross.
examples.cn: 这座桥归公众所有，过桥免费。

examples.en: The list is publicly available from next Monday.
examples.cn: 这份名单从下周一起可公开查阅。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「帕布立克力」——站到人人都立着看得见的地方去说去做，就是 publicly，公开地。

root: 拉丁语 populus（人民）→ publicus（属于人民的）→ 古法语 public → 英语 public；public 直接加副词后缀 -ly 得 publicly，义为「以公开、当众的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is doing something where everyone can see it; the senses divide into being watched, refusing to hide, being paid for by the public, and being reachable by anyone.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「在人人看得见的地方做事」；义项由此分为被观看、拒绝隐瞒、由公众出资，以及人人可取用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person on a platform holding a sheet above the head so the whole hall can see it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在台上，把一页纸举过头顶，让整个大厅都看见。

branches.en: a speaker facing a full hall without notes
branches.cn: 面对满场听众、不拿讲稿的发言者

branches.en: an admission made with the cameras running
branches.cn: 在摄像机开着时作出的承认

branches.en: a library whose bills are paid from taxes
branches.cn: 账单由税款支付的图书馆

branches.en: a file anyone may open on a public site
branches.cn: 任何人都能在公开网站上打开的文件

branches.en: the same openness turned towards truth and towards access
branches.cn: 同一种开放，一面朝向真相，一面朝向取用

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin noun for the people, the adjective public, and the English adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示人民的拉丁名词、形容词 public，以及英语副词后缀 -ly 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 出版；发表；公布；网络发布；刊登
definition_en: to make something public — first by announcing it, then by printing and selling it, and now by posting it online
core_image: 一扇原本关着的门被推开，屋里的话、文稿和消息一下子涌到街上，所有人都能听见看见
scene: 编辑指着屏幕安排今晚九点的上线时间。We publish the story at nine tonight.
sceneCN: 这里 publish 是「网络发布」（第 4 个义项：在网站或平台上发布内容）；句意：我们九点把报道发到网上，然后在任何人发现之前更新它。画面里有新闻编辑室、时钟和一个亮着的窗口；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 出版；发表；公布；发布；刊登

collocations.zh: 不发表就出局（学术界习语）

derivatives.zh: 出版者；出版商
出版；出版业
出版；出版物；发表
可出版的；适合发表的
